name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: The ab wheel roll-out is an exercise targeting the abdominals, often with an inexpensive wheel device with a handle on either side. Many trainers and strength coaches claim it's one of, if no the best exercise for developing strength in the midsection. Beginners may have to start with a limited range of motion or just wheel planks.

name: Air Bike
description: The air bike is a full-body conditioning machine that drives a fan with both the arms and the legs, so resistance scales with effort rather than with a dial. Short, hard intervals build work capacity while easy spinning serves as low-impact recovery. Keep the chest tall and push and pull the handles in rhythm with the pedals.

name: Archer Pull Ups
description: The archer pull up pulls the chest toward one hand while the opposite arm stays nearly straight, shifting almost the entire load onto the working side. Keep the straight arm from bending and pull the chin over the bent-arm hand; it is the bridge between regular pull ups and one-arm work.

name: Archer Push Ups
description: The archer push up lowers the chest toward one hand while the other arm slides out straight, loading one side of the chest far harder than a regular push up. Keep the straight arm honest and the hips square; it is the standard progression toward the one-arm push up.

name: Arnold Press
description: Named after the iconic bodybuilder and movie star, the Arnold press adds rotation to a classic shoulder press. It allows the hands to rotate naturally, while also hitting all three heads of the deltoids in one motion. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or more, as part of the upper-body or shoulder-focused portion of a workout.

name: Assisted Pull Ups
description: The assisted pull up uses a counterweighted machine to remove part of the bodyweight from the pull. Grip width and cues stay the same as a regular pull up; lighten the assist gradually over weeks and the first unassisted rep tends to follow.

name: Back Extension
description: The back extension is an exercise used to build lower back strength that also targets the hamstrings and glutes. It is often performed on a 45-degree bench with the feet anchored. Unweighted back extensions are often performed for high reps, such as 15-20 reps or more, but the movement can also be performed with added weight in lower rep ranges, such as 8-12 reps per set.

name: Back Lever
description: The back lever is an advanced gymnastics hold performed hanging from rings or a bar with the body turned face-down and extended horizontally. It demands strong lats, biceps and straight-arm strength along with shoulder mobility, so it is progressed through tucked and single-leg variations before the full position.

name: Ball Pike
description: The exercise ball pike is a challenging move that targets the core. It involves thrusting the hips into full flexion over a ball, then extending out to a foot-elevated plank with the feet on the ball. It's a challenging move from a strength perspective, but also for balance. It can be the centerpiece of an ab workout or go along with other body weight or ball movements in an ab circuit.

name: Band Assisted Pull Ups
description: The band-assisted pull-up is a variation of the pull-up exercise in which the reps are performed with an elastic band looped around the feet or knees. This reduces weight and resistance at the bottom of the rep, while increasing it toward the top. Like other pull-up variations, it builds strength and muscle in the upper back, biceps, and core, and is often used as a way to help people boost their pull-up numbers or perform their first rep.

name: Band Pull Apart
description: The band pull-apart is an exercise targeting the upper back muscles, including the trapezius, rear delts, and rhomboids. The band creates dynamic tension, allowing you to really focus on contracting these muscles, making it a great activation drill prior to upper-body lifting.

name: Banded Adductor Stretch
description: The banded adductor stretch loops a band around a straight leg and draws it out to the side while lying down, using the band to deepen the inner-thigh stretch. Keep the pelvis heavy on the floor and breathe into the tension; the band should pull, never yank.

name: Banded Ankle Stretch
description: The banded ankle stretch anchors a band over the ankle joint and drives the knee forward over the toes, mobilizing the ankle joint as the calf lengthens. The band's posterior pull is what makes this version work where a plain lean stalls; keep the heel down throughout.

name: Banded Calf Stretch
description: The banded calf stretch loops a band around the ball of the foot and pulls the toes back toward the shin with the leg straight. Keep the knee long to bias the gastrocnemius, then bend it slightly to reach the soleus; hold each version for 20 to 30 seconds.

name: Banded Chest Stretch
description: The banded chest stretch holds a band wide behind the back and lifts the arms, opening the pecs and front shoulders. Walk the grip narrower to intensify or raise the arms to change the line of pull; keep the ribs down rather than arching into it.

name: Banded Clamshell
description: The banded clamshell adds a band above the knees to the classic side-lying clamshell, forcing the glute medius to work against the band's pull. Keep the heels together and the pelvis still; the knee opens and nothing else moves.

name: Banded Figure-4 Stretch
description: The banded figure-4 stretch loops a band around one thigh and pulls the crossed ankle toward the chest while lying down, deepening the glute stretch. Keep the head and shoulders relaxed on the floor and let the band set the depth.

name: Banded Fire Hydrant
description: The banded fire hydrant lifts the knee sideways from a quadruped position against a band above the knees, targeting the glute medius. Keep the hips square to the floor and the torso quiet; small, controlled arcs beat big swings.

name: Banded Glute Bridge
description: The banded glute bridge bridges the hips up with a band pulling the knees inward, so the glutes must push out as well as extend. Keep the band under constant tension at the top and squeeze hard; the knees should track over the toes, never cave.

name: Banded Good Morning
description: The band good morning is an exercise targeting the hamstrings and glutes. It is often performed in powerlifting-style training for high reps, or in the place of barbell good mornings.

name: Banded Hamstring Stretch
description: The banded hamstring stretch lies on the back with a band looped around the foot and draws the straight leg toward the chest. Keep the other leg heavy on the floor and the knee of the working leg long; the band sets the depth, not the arm strength.

name: Banded Hip Thrust
description: The banded hip thrust drives the hips to extension against a band looped over the pelvis and anchored under the feet. The resistance rises exactly where the glutes are strongest, at lockout; tuck the pelvis and finish each rep with a hard squeeze.

name: Banded IT-Band Stretch
description: The banded IT-band stretch lies on the back with a band around the foot and draws the straight leg across the body toward the opposite shoulder. Keep the pelvis and the opposite shoulder heavy on the floor; the stretch should run down the outer thigh, not wrench the knee.

name: Banded Kneeling Hip Thrust
description: The banded kneeling hip thrust kneels tall with a band over the pelvis and pushes the hips forward to full extension, training the glutes in the standing hip-extension pattern. Keep the ribs down and squeeze the glutes to finish; the band's pull rises toward lockout.

name: Banded Lat Stretch
description: The banded lat stretch holds a band overhead and leans sideways, letting the band lengthen the lats along the ribs. Anchor the hips and keep both feet grounded; breathe into the stretched side and let the arm travel with the band rather than fighting it.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
description: The banded lateral walk side-steps against a band around the ankles or knees, keeping constant outward tension on the glute medius. Stay low in an athletic quarter squat and never let the knees cave between steps; equal distances each way.

name: Banded Rear Delt Stretch
description: The banded rear delt stretch crosses a band in front of the body and draws the arms across the chest, opening the back of the shoulders. Keep the neck relaxed and the shoulders down; a light, sustained pull does more than a hard yank.

name: Banded Romanian Deadlift
description: The banded Romanian deadlift hinges under a band anchored at the feet, where resistance increases through the lockout exactly as the glutes and hamstrings finish. Keep the spine long and push the hips back; the band makes the top of the rep the hardest part.

name: Banded Seated Hip Abduction
description: The banded seated hip abduction pushes the knees apart against a band while seated, isolating the upper glutes with nothing but a loop. Sit tall and keep the feet still; the knees travel and the torso does not.

name: Banded Shoulder Stretch
description: The banded shoulder stretch draws a band overhead and behind the back in a slow arc, opening the shoulders through their full range. Keep the elbows long and the grip adjustable, since narrower is harder; never force past a pinching shoulder.

name: Banded Squat
description: The banded squat squats against a band anchored under the feet and over the shoulders, so the load grows toward lockout where a barbell is easiest. Keep the chest tall and the knees tracking out; the band rewards full, smooth extensions.

name: Banded Standing Hip Abduction
description: The banded standing hip abduction swings the leg out to the side against an ankle band, training the glute medius in a standing posture. Keep the torso upright and square, since leaning away cheats the rep; the range is small and that is fine.

name: Banded Standing Hip Adduction
description: The banded standing hip adduction draws the leg across the body against a band anchored to the side, working the adductors from a standing base. Stand tall on the supporting leg and sweep slowly; the crossing leg does the work and the trunk stays quiet.

name: Banded Standing Leg Curl
description: The banded standing leg curl curls the heel toward the glute against an ankle-anchored band from a standing position, isolating the hamstrings of the working leg. Keep the thigh vertical and the hips square; control the return, as the band wants to snap the leg back.

name: Banded Sumo Walk
description: The banded sumo walk walks forward and backward in a wide, low stance against a band around the knees or ankles, keeping constant outward tension on the hips. Stay in the quarter squat the whole time; short, wide steps and level hips.

name: Banded Terminal Knee Extension
description: The banded terminal knee extension straightens the knee against a band pulling it backward, retraining the quad's final lockout after injury or long sitting. The band sits behind the knee and the heel stays down; the movement is small, precise and important.

name: Banded Triceps Stretch
description: The banded triceps stretch holds a band overhead in one hand and draws the elbow back with the other, lengthening the triceps behind the arm. Keep the ribs down and the neck long; a gentle sustained pull with slow breathing loosens the elbow's lockout range.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout
description: The barbell roll-out is an abdominal exercise that utilizes a barbell in the place of an ab roller. It is best performed with a barbell that has rotating collars, and is considered more difficult than other ab roller variations. Many lifters may not be able to perform a single rep at first, but once they can perform these for reps, they'll be rewarded with a seriously strong core.

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: The barbell back squat is a popular compound movement that emphasizes building the lower-body muscle groups and overall strength. It's the classic way to start a leg day, and is a worthy centerpiece to a lower-body training program. The squat is a competitive lift in the sport of powerlifting, but is also a classic measurement of lower-body strength. With the barbell racked on the traps or upper back, the emphasis is placed on the posterior chain but the entire body gets worked. The back squat can be trained in everything from heavy singles to sets of 20 reps or higher.

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: The bench press is a compound exercise that builds strength and muscle in the chest and triceps. When many people think of listing, the bench press is often the first exercise that comes to mind

name: Barbell Calf Raise
description: The barbell calf raise stands with a bar on the back and drives the heels up through a full ankle extension. Keep the knees straight to bias the gastrocnemius, pause at the top and lower slowly through the full stretch; balance near a rack for safety.

name: Barbell Curl
description: The barbell curl is an arm exercise that is also one of the most recognizable movements in all of bodybuilding and fitness. It helps build sleeve-popping biceps and allows heavier loading than many other curl variations. It is usually performed in moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set, as part of the arm-focused portion of any workout.

name: Barbell Deadlift
description: The barbell deadlift is a compound exercise used to develop overall strength and size in the posterior chain. It is a competition lift in the sport of powerlifting, but is also considered a classic benchmark of overall strength. When performed with the hands outside the knees, it is often called a \"conventional\" deadlift. When the feet are wide and the hands are inside the knees, it is a sumo deadlift.

name: Barbell Front Raise
description: The barbell front raise is an upper-body isolation exercise that targets the shoulders. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or higher, as part of the shoulder-focused part of any workout.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
description: The barbell glute bridge is a popular exercise targeting the muscles of the glutes and hamstrings. It can be done as a strength movement on its own, as an activation drill or warm-up for lower-body training, or as a burnout at the end of a lower-body workout.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: The barbell hip thrust is an exercise that engages the posterior chain, particular the glutes. It involves fully extending your hips while holding a weighted barbell across the midsection.

name: Barbell Lunge
description: The barbell forward lunge is a popular lower-body exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. Using a barbell allows you to overload the exercise beyond body weight and perform the movement in strength or muscle-focused rep ranges. The forward lunge can be performed as part of a barbell complex, in a circuit, or on its own in the lower-body portion of any workout.

name: Barbell Overhead Extension
description: The barbell overhead extension lowers a bar behind the head from a locked-out overhead grip and extends it back up, working the long head of the triceps through a deep stretch. Keep the elbows pointing forward and narrow, and the ribs down.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
description: The barbell overhead press presses a barbell from the shoulders to lockout with the legs quiet, the purest measure of upper-body pressing strength. Squeeze the glutes to lock the torso, move the head back out of the bar's path and finish with the bar over the mid-foot.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
description: The reverse-grip barbell curl is a variation on the biceps curl where the palms face downward. The switch from an underhand to an overhand grip brings the forearm and brachialis muscles more into the exercise. If it is uncomfortable to the wrists, try performing it on the angles of an EZ-curl bar.

name: Barbell Pullover
description: The barbell pullover arcs a bar from over the chest to behind the head and back while lying on a bench, stretching the lats and chest under load. Keep the elbows slightly bent and the hips steady; the movement happens at the shoulders, not the spine.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
description: The barbell rear delt row rows a barbell high toward the chest with the elbows flared wide, biasing the rear delts and upper back over the lats. Hinge to near-parallel and keep the neck long; think of pulling with the elbows, not the hands.

name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
description: The barbell reverse lunge is a popular lower-body exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. Using a barbell allows you to overload the exercise beyond body weight and perform the movement in strength or muscle-focused rep ranges. The reverse lunge can be performed as part of a barbell complex, in a circuit, or on its own in the lower-body portion of any workout.

name: Barbell Shrug
description: The barbell shrug is an exercise targeting the traps (trapezius muscles). It is popular in strength and muscle-focused upper-body training, and is often trained on a shoulder day. With the assistance of straps, it can be loaded heavily, but it is still usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-10 reps per set.

name: Barbell Upright Row
description: The barbell upright row is a barbell exercise that builds stronger and bigger traps. Many lifters combine this move with either their back or shoulder workout since it involves both body parts.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl
description: The barbell wrist curl rests the forearms on a bench or the thighs and hinges the wrists to curl the bar up, training the forearm flexors. Use a modest weight and a full range, from fully extended fingers to full flexion; slow negatives build the grip fastest.

name: Battle Rope Double Slam
description: The battle rope double slam drives both ropes overhead and slams them to the floor in one explosive motion, training the shoulders, core and hips as a single chain. It is usually performed for time or high reps, making it a staple of conditioning circuits and metabolic finishers.

name: Battle Ropes
description: Battle ropes are an explosive training tool that involves moving the rope in waves with the other end of the rope anchored at ground level. There are many different types of waves, but the most common is alternating waves with the left and right hands. The battle ropes can be performed for short bursts as power training, for longer durations as cardiovascular training, or as a component of a conditioning or fat-loss circuit.

name: Bear Crawl
description: The bear crawl is a popular bodyweight crawling exercise. While it looks simple, the bear crawl is an intense full-body movement that targets the cardiovascular system as well as a wide range of muscle groups, the shoulders, core, and legs in particular. It can be done as a full-body warm-up, in short bursts for power or circuit training, or for longer durations as cardiovascular conditioning.

name: Behind the Back Barbell Shrug
description: The barbell behind-the-back shrug is an exercise targeting the traps. Having the bar behind you helps keep your shoulders pulled up and back, rather than rounded forward. It is popular in strength and muscle-focused upper-body training, and is often trained on a shoulder day. With the assistance of straps, it can be loaded heavily, but it is still usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-10 reps per set.

name: Behind the Neck Press
description: The behind-the-neck press presses a barbell from behind the head to lockout, demanding exceptional shoulder mobility. It builds the overhead position powerfully but is unforgiving of tight shoulders; only press from behind the neck if the bar can travel there without the head jutting forward.

name: Behind-the-Neck Lat Pulldown
description: The behind-the-neck pull-down is a cable exercise intended to target the muscles of the upper and middle back. If you have the requisite shoulder mobility, it can help you target the upper back muscles, including the trapezius and rhomboids, as well as the lats (latissimus dorsi). It is popular among elite bodybuilders and physique athletes, but some coaches consider it unsafe to the shoulder joint, particularly for people with existing shoulder problems.

name: Behind-the-Neck Pull-Up
description: The behind-the-neck pull up pulls the bar down behind the head, an old-school variation that demands mobile shoulders and precise control. Only pull to a point behind the head without craning the neck forward; if the shoulders pinch or the head juts, stay with front pull ups.

name: Bench Adductor Stretch
description: The bench adductor stretch opens the inner thighs by placing one leg on a bench and folding the torso toward it. Keep the standing knee soft and hinge from the hips rather than rounding the back, easing into the stretch until the adductors release.

name: Bench Ankle Stretch
description: The bench ankle stretch improves dorsiflexion by placing the ball of one foot on a bench and driving the knee forward over the toes. Keep the heel down and the movement slow, using short pulsing leans to loosen a stiff ankle before squatting or lunging.

name: Bench Bulgarian Split Stretch
description: The bench Bulgarian split stretch lengthens the hip flexors of the rear leg by draping that foot on a bench behind you and sinking the hips down and forward. Squeeze the rear glute to deepen the stretch safely; it doubles as the setup position for Bulgarian split squats.

name: Bench Calf Stretch
description: The bench calf stretch places the forefoot on a bench with the heel anchored to the floor, then leans the torso in to lengthen the calf. Straighten the knee to bias the gastrocnemius or bend it slightly to reach the soleus.

name: Bench Chest Stretch
description: The bench chest stretch lies face-up across a bench with the arms opened wide, letting gravity pull the shoulders toward the floor. It is a gentle way to open a tight chest after pressing work; bend the elbows more to shift the emphasis toward the shoulders.

name: Bench Child's Pose
description: The bench child's pose kneels in front of a bench and folds the arms onto it, lengthening the lats and spine without loading the knees. Breathe slowly into the sides of the ribcage and let the hips sink back with each exhale.

name: Bench Couch Stretch
description: The bench couch stretch is a quad and hip-flexor opener that sets the rear foot up on a bench behind the body, then raises the torso upright. Tuck the pelvis and squeeze the rear glute before leaning back; it is one of the most effective stretches for desk-tightened hips.

name: Bench Dips
description: The bench dip is a highly effective exercise for building the triceps. The resistance comes from the body itself, rather than weight.

name: Bench Figure-4 Glute Stretch
description: The bench figure-4 glute stretch crosses one ankle over the opposite knee in a seated position and folds forward, stretching the glutes and hip rotators. Keep the back long rather than rounded and pull the crossed knee gently toward the chest to intensify it.

name: Bench Hamstring Stretch
description: The bench hamstring stretch rests one straight leg on a bench and hinges the chest toward the thigh. Keep both hips square and the knee of the elevated leg unlocked to target the hamstring without straining its attachments.

name: Bench Lat Stretch
description: The bench lat stretch grips a bench with both hands and sinks the hips back and down, letting the torso fall between the arms. Push the chest toward the floor and rotate the palms slightly outward to widen the stretch through the lats.

name: Bench Leg Pull-In
description: The bench leg pull-in sits on a bench and pulls the knees in toward the chest and back out, training the abs through a long, controlled range. Grip the bench for stability and keep the lower back from rounding at the extension; slow beats fast.

name: Bench Pull
description: The bench pull lies chest-down on a high bench and rows a barbell from beneath it, removing all body English from the pull. The chest stays planted so the lats and mid-back do the work; pull the bar to the underside of the bench and lower with control.

name: Bent Arm Barbell Pullover
description: The bent-arm barbell pull-over was a staple exercise of the \"Golden Era\" of bodybuilding and a favorite of Arnold Schwarzenegger himself. Done properly, the exercise targets the pecs, lats, and serratus anterior muscles. Old-school bodybuilders would perform them with light weights for sets of 20 between sets of heavy 20-rep squats, but pull-overs are more popular today in moderate rep ranges, such as 8-12 reps per set, as part of an upper-body workout.

name: Bent-Arm EZ-Bar Pullover
description: The bent-arm EZ-bar pullover lies on a bench and arcs the bar from over the chest to behind the head with the elbows bent, easing the demand on the shoulders while still stretching the lats and chest. Keep the elbows pointing up and the ribs down throughout.

name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
description: The barbell bent-over row is a compound exercise used to build strength and size in both the lower and upper back. It targets nearly all of the muscles in the back, but particularly the lats, rhomboids, and lower back. It is commonly utilized as an accessory movement for the deadlift in powerlifting, but is also popular in strength and muscle-focused upper-body workouts.

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row
description: The dumbbell bent-over row is a popular exercise to develop and strengthen the muscles of the upper and middle back, like the latissimus (lat), lower trapezius, and rear deltoids. It can work equally well in strength, muscle-building, or circuit-style fat-loss workouts.

name: Bent-Over EZ-Bar Row
description: The bent-over EZ-bar row hinges forward and rows the angled bar to the lower ribs, the EZ grip turning the wrists into a more natural position for many lifters. Keep the torso close to parallel and drive the elbows past the ribs.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: The bicycle crunch alternates bringing the opposite elbow toward the knee while the other leg extends, rotating through the trunk continuously. Keep the lower back light on the floor and rotate from the ribs rather than swinging the elbows; moderate speed, full rotation.

name: Bilateral Dumbbell Wrist Curl
description: The bilateral dumbbell wrist curl curls both wrists together from a braced position, training the forearm flexors symmetrically. Keep the range full, from fingers hanging open to full flexion; light bells and high reps suit the wrists best.

name: Bird Dog Hold
description: The bird dog is a core exercise designed to help strengthen and stabilize the posterior chain. It involves lifting an opposite-side arm and leg while in a bent-leg tabletop position. It is most commonly performed as part of a dynamic warm-up, or for mobility and muscle activation anytime.

name: Bird-Dog
description: The bird dog is a core exercise designed to help strengthen and stabilize the posterior chain. It involves lifting an opposite-side arm and leg while in a bent-leg tabletop position. It is most commonly performed as part of a dynamic warm-up, or for mobility and muscle activation anytime.

name: Boat Pose
description: Boat pose is a yoga hold that balances on the sitting bones with the legs and torso forming a V. It builds isometric strength through the deep abdominals and hip flexors; keep the chest lifted and the spine long rather than rounding to bring the legs higher.

name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
description: The bodyweight calf raise drives the heels up from the floor through a full ankle extension, training the calves with nothing but bodyweight. Pause at the top and lower through the full stretch; hold a wall for balance but not for assistance.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
description: The bodyweight good morning hinges at the hips with the hands behind the head or at the chest, loading the hamstrings and lower back through a slow, deliberate bow. Keep the spine long and the knees soft; it is a warm-up and hinge-pattern drill rather than a strength lift.

name: Bodyweight Lateral Raise
description: The bodyweight lateral raise raises the arms out to the sides with no added load, cueing the side delts in warm-ups and mobility work. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears; think of it as motor-pattern rehearsal for the loaded version.

name: Bodyweight Overhead Press
description: The bodyweight overhead press stands and presses the arms overhead with no load, rehearsing the shoulder press pattern in warm-ups and mobility work. Keep the ribs down and reach tall at the top; it is a pattern primer, not a strength builder.

name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
description: The reverse lunge is a lower-body exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. The reverse lunge places more emphasis on the glutes than other lunge variations.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: The bodyweight squat is a fundamental exercise that strengthens the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. It can be performed as part of a dynamic warm-up, for time or reps during a workout, or for hip and spine mobility any time.

name: Bow Pose
description: Bow pose lies face-down, bends the knees and reaches back to grip the ankles, lifting the chest and thighs into an arch. It stretches the front of the body while strengthening the spinal erectors; keep the knees hip-width and avoid forcing the lift.

name: Box Jump
description: The box jump is an explosive exercise that strengthens the muscles of the lower body, including the quads, glutes, calves, and hamstrings. They also develop power in the lower body while revving the heart rate. Box jumps can be performed for low reps to focus on strength and power, or for higher reps for metabolic conditioning. Most coaches recommend stepping down rather than jumping down between reps.

name: Box Squat
description: The box squat squats back onto a box or bench, touching it briefly before driving up, which sets the depth and teaches the hip hinge. Sit back fully, keep the shins near vertical and stay braced through the touch; drive up without rocking forward.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: The barbell Bulgarian split squat is a single-leg exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. It is easier to overload with the barbell than when using dumbbells. If balance is an issue, consider using a Smith machine or holding dumbbells at your side instead.

name: Burpees
description: The burpee is a high-intensity exercise that recruits the entire body to build strength and aerobic capacity. It is common in CrossFit workouts and group fitness classes, but can also be performed for time or reps in any fat-loss or athleticism-focused circuit or workout.

name: Butterfly Stretch
description: The butterfly stretch sits with the soles of the feet together and lets the knees fall toward the floor, opening the inner thighs and groin. Keep the spine long and hinge slightly from the hips rather than rounding; pressing gently on the knees deepens the stretch, and never bounce.

name: Cable Bent-Over Row
description: The cable bent-over row hinges forward and rows a cable attachment to the lower ribs, pulling against constant resistance through the whole range. The cable's line differs from a barbell, so the lats and mid-back work without lower-back compression; keep the torso steady and the elbows driving back.

name: Cable Chest Press
description: The cable chest press presses two handles forward from the chest from a standing or seated stance. The cables pull slightly apart through the press, so the pecs stabilize as well as push; step into a staggered stance and keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.

name: Cable Crunch
description: The kneeling cable crunch is a popular core isolation exercise using a rope attachment and cable stack while kneeling on the floor. It primarily targets the rectus abdominus or \"six-pack\" muscles, but also strengthens the deep core muscles. It is most commonly performed early in an ab workout, usually in moderate to high reps like 8-12 reps per set or higher.

name: Cable Curl
description: The cable curl curls a handle or bar from a low pulley, keeping tension on the biceps at both the top and the bottom of every rep. Keep the elbows pinned to the sides and resist the weight on the way down; the constant load is the point.

name: Cable External Rotation
description: The cable external rotation rotates the upper arm outward against a low cable with the elbow pinned at the side, training the rotator cuff directly. Go light, since this is a precision drill rather than a strength showcase; control the return slowly.

name: Cable Face Pull
description: The standing face pull is an isolation exercise primarily targeting the rear deltoids, traps, and upper back. It is most often performed with a rope attachment.

name: Cable Fly
description: The cable fly sweeps two pulley handles together in a wide arc in front of the chest, loading the pecs through constant tension. Keep a soft, fixed elbow bend and let the arms draw the arc from the shoulders; squeeze the hands together at the front for a beat.

name: Cable Front Raise
description: The lying cable front raise is an isolation exercise for the shoulders, particularly the front deltoids. It is performed lying on the back, either on a bench or the ground, with the cable lifted over the torso. This movement is usually performed for moderate to high reps for a burn and pump as part of a shoulder-focused workout.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
description: The cable glute kickback extends the leg straight back against an ankle cuff from a low pulley, isolating the glute of the working hip. Keep the torso square to the machine; the temptation to arch is what the drill trains away. Squeeze the glute to finish, not the lower back.

name: Cable Hammer Curl
description: The cable rope hammer curl is a popular arm-focused exercise performed with a rope handle attached by a cable to a weight stack. It uses a neutral (palms facing one another) grip, which targets the forearms and brachialis muscles in addition to the biceps. Because grip is a limitation, it is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: The cable lateral raise raises one arm out to the side against a low pulley, loading the side delt with tension from the very first degree. Keep the elbow slightly bent and the torso still; the cable's constant pull makes lighter weights feel honest.

name: Cable Pallof Press
description: The pallof press is an anti-rotation, isometric exercise that trains core stability. It is most often seen in programs for athletes who compete in sports that test strength, power, and functional movements.

name: Cable Tricep Kickback
description: The cable tricep kickback hinges forward and extends the forearm back against a low cable, keeping tension on the triceps through the entire arc. Pin the upper arm parallel to the floor and let only the forearm move; the cable fixes the sagging resistance of the dumbbell version.

name: Cable Tricep Pushdown
description: The cable tricep pushdown extends the arms down against a high pulley, the staple triceps isolation with constant resistance. Pin the elbows to the ribs and split the hands slightly at the bottom; control the return rather than letting the stack fall.

name: Cable Upright Row
description: The cable upright row pulls a bar or rope up the front of the body from a low pulley, training the side delts and upper traps. Keep the hands no wider than the shoulders and stop at chest height; the cable keeps the load smooth where a barbell jars.

name: Cable Wrist Curl
description: The cable wrist curl flexes the wrists against a low cable with the forearms braced on the thighs or a bench. Constant tension makes even light weights effective; use full range and high reps for the flexors.

name: Camel Pose
description: Camel pose kneels upright and reaches back to the heels, opening the chest and shoulders into a deep backbend. Press the hips forward over the knees and keep the glutes engaged so the bend comes from the upper back rather than hinging at the lumbar spine.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
description: The captain's chair knee raise is a bodyweight exercise that targets the abs. It is performed on an apparatus that allows the forearms to rest on pads and the upright torso to hang freely. Knee raises are often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or more, as part of ab-focused training.

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
description: The captain's chair leg raise is a bodyweight exercise that targets the abs. It is performed on an apparatus that allows the forearms to rest on pads and the upright torso to hang freely. Leg raise variations are often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or more, as part of ab-focused training.

name: Cat Stretch
description: The cat stretch rounds and arches the spine on all fours in a slow, controlled rhythm. It mobilizes the whole vertebral column and re-establishes awareness of the core; sync each movement with a full breath cycle.

name: Cat-Cow
description: Cat-cow is a traditional yoga pose that is also popular in fitness and strength training. It targets spinal mobility and control of the vertebral column. It can be performed for time or reps as part of a dynamic warm-up or as a mobility or restorative exercise anytime. It can also work as part of a yoga or bodyweight sequence with other poses.

name: Chair Pose
description: Chair pose holds a deep quarter squat with the arms overhead, loading the quads, glutes and shoulders isometrically. Sit the hips back, keep the weight in the heels and draw the lower ribs in so the back stays long.

name: Cheat Curl
description: The cheat curl uses a controlled body swing to start a heavier-than-strict barbell curl, then fights the lowering with pure biceps. The cheat is the setup, not the rep, and the eccentric must stay strict; it is an advanced overload tool, not a permission slip to swing every curl.

name: Chest Dips
description: The chest dip is a chest-building exercise in which the lifter hangs between two parallel handles. Leaning the torso slightly forward shifts the emphasis from the triceps to the chest.

name: Chest Supported Dumbbell Shrug
description: The chest-supported dumbbell shrug shrugs two heavy bells from a chest-down position on an incline bench, isolating the traps without the lower back in the equation. Keep the arms long and lift the shoulders toward the ears; a brief hold at the top does the work.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
description: The chest-supported dumbbell row rows two bells from an incline bench with the chest pinned to the pad, removing every trace of body English. Pull the elbows past the ribs and squeeze the shoulder blades; the bells hang fully at the bottom of each rep.

name: Chest-Supported Kettlebell Row
description: The chest-supported kettlebell row rows two bells from an incline bench with the chest pinned, taking all momentum out of the pull. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top and let the arms hang fully at the bottom; the back, not the arms, should ache after.

name: Chest-Supported Smith Machine Row
description: The chest-supported Smith machine row sets an incline bench under the bar so the chest stays pinned while the arms row. The pad removes all cheating from the pull; squeeze the shoulder blades at the top and let the elbows drive past the ribs.

name: Child's Pose
description: Child’s pose is a traditional yoga pose that is also popular in fitness and strength training. It targets mobility of the thoracic spine and control of the vertebral column. It can be performed for time or reps as part of a dynamic warm-up or as a mobility or restorative exercise anytime. It can also work as part of a yoga or bodyweight sequence with other poses.

name: Chin Tuck Hold
description: The chin tuck hold lies on the back and gently draws the chin toward the throat, holding the position to strengthen the deep neck flexors. It is a common corrective for forward-head posture and is usually held for 15 to 30 seconds at a time.

name: Chin-Ups
description: The a chin-up is a variation of the pull-up exercise in which the reps are performed with the palms facing toward the body, in an underhand position, with a grip that is narrower than shoulder-width. Like other pull-up variations, it builds strength and muscle in the upper back, biceps, and core, but it utilizes the biceps slightly more than overhand pull-ups. It can be used as a more shoulder-friendly alternative to straight-bar pull-ups, or to help perform more reps than you can perform overhand.

name: Clamshell Hold
description: The clamshell hold keeps the top knee of a side-lying clamshell open and suspended, turning the exercise into an isometric for the hip abductors. The leg should stay light; if the pelvis rocks backward, the glute is no longer doing the work.

name: Clamshells
description: The clamshell lies on the side with the heels together and opens the top knee like a shell, training the glute medius through its smallest but most important job. Keep the pelvis perfectly still; if the hip rolls back, the glute has handed off the work.

name: Clap Push-Ups
description: The clap push-up presses up explosively enough for the hands to leave the floor and clap before the next rep, developing upper-body power. Land with soft elbows and keep the body in one plank throughout; fall back to regular push-ups the moment the landings turn sloppy.

name: Clean
description: The clean pulls a barbell from the floor to the shoulders in one explosive motion, catching it on the front delts in a quarter squat. It develops triple-extension power through the hips, knees and ankles unlike any slow lift; the pull is vertical and the elbows whip under fast.

name: Clean and Jerk
description: The clean and jerk is a full-body lift that is one of two contested lifts in Olympic weightlifting competitions. It is comprised of two movements: the clean, where the bar is pulled from the floor and caught in the front rack position in three pulls or phases, followed by the jerk overhead. The clean and jerk hits every muscle from head to toe and can be the centerpiece of a lifting program. It is also popular in CrossFit and athletic training programs. It is usually performed in low rep ranges, focusing on power and movement quality.

name: Close Grip Lat Pulldown
description: The close-grip pull-down is a variation on the lat pull-down, acable-based exercise machine that’s ubiquitous in gyms around the world. This back builder is easy to learn and highly effective, allowing for variable resistance depending on where you place the pin in the stack.

name: Close Grip Push Ups
description: The close-grip push up keeps the hands directly under the shoulders or narrower, shifting the load from the chest toward the triceps. Keep the elbows brushing the ribs on the way down; the body stays in one line exactly as in a regular push up.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Curl
description: The close-grip barbell curl is a curl variation where the hands are closer than shoulder width. It is thought that this helps build the outer biceps head and the peak. This curl variation is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
description: The close-grip bench press is a popular exercise targeting the triceps and chest. The main difference between this exercise and the standard bench press is that the hands and elbows are placed closer together, which places more of an emphasis on the triceps. The close-grip bench press is often used as an accessory movement for the traditional bench press, or as a triceps builder for arm training. Similar to the bench press, it can be trained in low reps for strength or higher reps for muscle or strength endurance.

name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
description: The close-grip dumbbell bench press is a popular variation of the dumbbell bench press in which the dumbbells are held closer than shoulder width. This places more emphasis on the triceps, and perhaps also the inner chest. The close-grip dumbbell bench press can be performed in lower reps for strength or higher reps for muscle growth.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Bench Press
description: The close-grip EZ-bar bench press is an exercise targeting the chest, shoulders, and triceps. This move is more commonly done with a straight bar and is often only performed with an EZ-bar as part of a complex of movements such as pull-overs or skullcrushers.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl
description: The close-grip EZ-bar curl is an exercise targeting the biceps, particularly the long head. The main difference between this exercise and standard EZ-bar curls is that the hands are positioned closer together on the bar. It is thought that this helps build the outer biceps head and the peak. This curl variation is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set.

name: Close-Grip Incline Bench Press
description: The close-grip incline bench press presses from an incline bench with the hands inside shoulder width, stacking the triceps and upper chest together. Keep the elbows tucked close to the torso and touch the bar just below the collar line.

name: Close-Grip Pull-Ups
description: The close-grip pull up hangs with the hands nearly touching and pulls the chest to the bar, shifting the load toward the lower lats and biceps. Keep the shoulders from shrugging and drive the elbows down toward the hips; the narrow grip asks more of the arms.

name: Close-Stance Leg Press
description: The close-stance leg press places the feet hip-width and low on the platform, shifting the emphasis toward the quads. Keep the lower back glued to the pad and stop the set when the pelvis starts to tuck; depth is useful, lumbar rounding is not.

name: Cobra Stretch
description: The cobra stretch lies face-down and presses the chest up with straight arms or a gentle lift, opening the abdominals and hip flexors. Keep the shoulders away from the ears and let the neck stay neutral; small doses after sitting or heavy squats feel best.

name: Cocoons
description: The cocoon crunch is a bodyweight exercise targeting the ab muscles, the rectus abdominis or \"six-pack\" muscles in particular. It involves bringing your knees to your chest and your arms from overhead to center. It can be performed for time or reps as part of the ab-focused portion of any workout.

name: Concentration Curl
description: The concentration curl is a classic exercise for building the biceps one arm at a time. It can be performed bent over or kneeling, but is more often performed seated on a bench. It's great for emphasizing the biceps peak and is often used to finish a biceps workout. Like most curl variations, these are usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more.

name: Corpse Pose
description: Corpse pose lies flat on the back with the limbs heavy and the breath slow. It closes a session by dropping the heart rate and releasing residual tension; the discipline is doing nothing deliberately, scanning and softening the body piece by piece.

name: Cossack Squat
description: The Cossack squat sinks sideways onto one loaded leg while the other leg extends out long, training the quads, adductors and ankle mobility at once. Keep the working heel down and the chest up; go only as deep as the hips and ankle allow without collapsing.

name: Cow Face Pose
description: Cow face pose stacks the knees and binds the hands behind the back, opening the outer hips and shoulders at the same time. Use a strap if the hands cannot meet, and switch sides to keep both hips even.

name: Crab Dips
description: The crab dip lowers the body from a reverse tabletop position by bending the elbows, training the triceps through an unusual shoulder extension angle. Keep the hips high and the elbows tracking straight back; the shoulders should open, not shrug toward the ears.

name: Crescent Lunge
description: The crescent lunge holds a deep forward lunge with the back knee lifted and the arms reaching overhead. It opens the hip flexors of the rear leg while the front leg and core hold the balance; keep the front knee stacked over the ankle.

name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
description: The cross-body hammer curl is a dumbbell exercise that targets the biceps, brachialis, and forearm muscles. Rather than lifting the weights directly in front of the body, you lift them across the torso. Throughout each rep, the wrists remain neutral, like a carpenter hammering a nail. This helps isolate the brachialis muscles on each arm. It is generally performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or more, as part of the arm-focused portion of a workout.

name: Cross-Body Crunch
description: The elbow-to-knee crunch is a bodyweight exercise targeting the ab muscles, the obliques and rectus abdominis or \"six-pack\" muscles in particular. It can be performed for time or reps as part of the ab-focused portion of any workout.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
description: The cross-body shoulder stretch targets increased flexibility in the shoulders. It is a common inclusion in upper-body dynamic warm-ups prior to training or sports, but can also be performed anytime to \"limber up\" the upper body.

name: Crow Pose
description: Crow pose balances the shins on the backs of the upper arms with the feet off the floor, training shoulder stability, wrist strength and core control. Start with one foot at a time or a block under the toes; look slightly forward, not straight down.

name: Crunches
description: The crunch is a popular core exercise targeting the rectus abdominis, or \"six-pack\" muscles, as well as the obliques. It has been the centerpiece of many ab-focused workouts, due to both its simplicity and the intense burn and mind-muscle connection it produces. It can be performed for time or reps as part of the ab-focused portion of any workout.

name: Dancer Pose
description: Dancer pose balances on one leg while holding the opposite foot behind the body, kicking the lifted leg into the hand to open the quad and shoulder. Fix the gaze on a point and hinge the torso forward gradually; it challenges balance as much as flexibility.

name: Dead Bug
description: The dead bug lies on the back and slowly extends the opposite arm and leg away from the trunk while the lower back stays pressed to the floor. It teaches the core to hold position while the limbs move; move slowly enough that nothing else on the body wobbles.

name: Dead Bug Hold
description: The dead bug hold keeps the opposite arm and leg hovering off the floor in a static version of the dead bug. Press the lower back into the ground throughout; the moment it arches, the range is too long for the core to control.

name: Dead Hang
description: The dead hang simply hangs from a pull-up bar with straight arms, building grip strength, shoulder health and the lat mobility needed for pulling work. Let the shoulders rise toward the ears at the start and settle into a relaxed, active hang.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
description: The decline barbell bench press is a popular upper-body exercise targeting the lower pectoral muscles. While it can be a strength-focused movement, it is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of upper-body or chest-focused training.

name: Decline Bench Press
description: The decline barbell bench press is a popular upper-body exercise targeting the lower pectoral muscles. While it can be a strength-focused movement, it is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of upper-body or chest-focused training.

name: Decline Crunch
description: The decline crunch is an effective core exercise targeting the rectus abdominis.

name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
description: The decline dumbbell chest fly is an upper body isolation exercise targeting the lower chest. It will require less weight than a decline press, which makes it a great hypertrophy exercise with high reps.

name: Decline EZ-Bar Bench Press
description: The decline EZ-bar bench press presses from a decline bench with the angled bar, biasing the lower chest while easing shoulder strain. Keep the feet hooked, the bar path over the lower chest and the elbows about 45 degrees from the torso.

name: Decline Push-Up
description: The feet-elevated push-up is a variation on the push-up, a body-weight standard. The feet are elevated, so that your body is aligned at an angle to the floor rather than parallel.

name: Deficit Deadlift
description: The barbell deficit deadlift is a compound exercise targeting the posterior chain.

name: Deficit Push Ups
description: The deficit push up places the hands on blocks or dumbbells, letting the chest sink below hand level for a longer range. Keep the body in one line through the deeper bottom; the extra stretch is the growth, and the reason the reps get hard fast.

name: Diamond Push Ups
description: The diamond push-up is an advanced variation of the push-up exercise performed with the hands in a diamond shape. It increases the challenge to the triceps, but also targets the chest and shoulders.

name: Dolphin Pose
description: Dolphin pose sets up like downward dog but rests on the forearms, shifting the load into the shoulders and upper back. It is the standard strength drill behind headstand and forearm-stand progressions; press the floor away and keep the ribs knitted in.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
description: The donkey calk raise is a strength and muscle-building exercise focused on the muscles of the lower leg, most prominently the gastrocnemius muscle. While traditional donkey calf raises involved either a specific machine or carrying another person on one's back, this method uses a weight belt. It can be done in traditional muscle-building rep ranges, or for higher reps as part of lower-body training.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
description: The doorway chest stretch places the forearms on a door frame and steps through until the chest opens. Elbow height decides the emphasis, lower for the lower chest and higher for the shoulders, so it is a quick, equipment-light fix for rounded posture.

name: Double Dumbbell Kickstand Deadlift
description: The double dumbbell kickstand deadlift hinges with two bells and one foot's toe kicked back behind the other, a hybrid between bilateral and single-leg work. The rear toe is a balance point only; load the front leg, push the hips back and keep both bells hugging the shins.

name: Double Dumbbell Overhead Carry
description: The double dumbbell overhead carry walks with a bell locked out in each hand, pressing the shoulders and core to hold the ribcage down under two loads. Keep the biceps near the ears and the steps short; the carry ends when the lockout starts to drift.

name: Double Kettlebell Bicep Curl
description: The double kettlebell bicep curl curls two bells together or alternately, front-loading the frame and doubling the grip demand. Keep the elbows pinned and the wrists neutral; the racked start position is half the core workout.

name: Double Kettlebell Clean
description: The double kettlebell clean drives two bells from the swing into the rack in one hip-powered motion. It is the gateway to double presses and front squats; punch the hands through rather than muscling the bells around the wrists.

name: Double Kettlebell Clean and Press
description: The double kettlebell clean and press chains a clean of both bells into a strict overhead press of both, then returns them under control. It is a brutal full-body strength and conditioning lift; every rep should start and end with crisp rack positions.

name: Double Kettlebell Dead Clean
description: The double kettlebell dead clean starts with both bells dead on the floor and cleans them to the rack in one pull. Starting from a dead stop removes the swing, so the pull is pure hip power; reset the setup each rep for the strictest version.

name: Double Kettlebell Dead Split Snatch
description: The double kettlebell dead split snatch pulls two dead bells from the floor and drives them overhead with a split stance catch. It is an advanced, explosive full-body lift; master the double clean and the split jerk separately before blending them.

name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
description: The double kettlebell jerk drives two racked bells overhead with a short dip and a punch of the legs, catching with straight arms. It moves far more load than the strict press and taxes the whole body; keep the dip shallow and the catch fast.

name: Double Kettlebell Overhead Carry
description: The double kettlebell overhead carry walks with a bell locked out in each hand, doubling the stability demand of the single version. The core must hold the ribcage down while the shoulders hold the lockout; short, frequent sets beat sloppy long ones.

name: Double Kettlebell Overhead Press
description: The double kettlebell overhead press presses two racked bells strictly overhead, loading the shoulders, triceps and trunk symmetrically. Keep the wrists stacked and the ribs down; the legs are quiet, as this is a press, not a push.

name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
description: The double-kettlebell push-press is a popular kettlebell movement that involves performing a press with help from the muscles of the lower body. It is preceded by a double clean at the start of each set, and optionally you can perform a clean between each rep. It can be trained in traditional strength or muscle-building rep ranges, in circuit or fat-loss training, or as part of a larger kettlebell combination or complex.

name: Double Kettlebell Rear Delt Row
description: The double kettlebell rear delt row hinges forward and rows two bells high toward the chest with the elbows flared. The wide pull biases the rear delts and upper back; keep the torso close to parallel and the neck long.

name: Double Kettlebell Row
description: The double kettlebell row hinges and rows two bells to the ribs together, loading the lats and grip symmetrically. Keep the back flat and let the hips and core hold the hinge; the bells' pull makes balance part of the exercise.

name: Double Kettlebell Split Jerk
description: The double kettlebell split jerk drives two racked bells overhead with a dip and a split-leg catch, the most load the overhead press family can move. Drop under the bells rather than pressing them up; recover the feet in order: front, back, together.

name: Double Kettlebell Swing Snatch
description: The double kettlebell swing snatch sends two swinging bells overhead in one violent, hip-driven motion. It is among the most demanding kettlebell lifts; own the double swing and double clean first, and expect the grip to give out before the hips do.

name: Downward Dog Knee Tuck
description: The downward dog knee tuck pulls one knee toward the chest from a downward dog, blending a hamstring stretch with a core crunch. Keep the shoulders stacked over the wrists and round the spine as the knee draws in; alternate sides with control.

name: Downward Dog Pedal
description: The downward dog pedal bends one knee while straightening the other in a slow alternating rhythm, warming the calves and hamstrings inside the downward dog position. It is a staple early stretch before lower-body training.

name: Downward Dog to Knee Drive
description: The downward dog to knee drive pulls one knee toward the opposite elbow from a downward dog, blending a rotation crunch with a hamstring stretch of the standing leg. Keep the shoulders stacked over the wrists and let the spine round as the knee drives across.

name: Downward Dog to Low Lunge
description: This flow steps one foot from downward dog into a low lunge and back, opening the hip flexors of the trailing leg and the hamstrings of the leading one. Move with the breath and keep the transitions smooth; it is an ideal warm-up sequence before squats or runs.

name: Downward Dog to Plank
description: The downward dog to plank flow rocks between the inverted V and the top of a push-up, training shoulder stability and core control in one smooth line. Keep the ribs knitted and the shoulders away from the ears in both positions; move with the breath.

name: Downward Dog to Upward Dog
description: The downward dog to upward dog flow sweeps from the inverted V through a low push-up into the chest-open backbend and back. Keep the shoulders down and the thighs hovering in the upward phase; it trains shoulder strength and spine extension together.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
description: Downward-facing dog forms an inverted V with the body, stretching the calves and hamstrings while the shoulders and arms bear weight. Press the floor away, reach the hips back and let the heels drift toward the ground rather than forcing them down.

name: Drag Curl
description: The drag curl is a biceps exercise that attempts to remove the influence of the front deltoids on the classic curl. With the elbows kept back, the barbell \"drags\" up the torso. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-15 reps per set, as part of an upper-body or arms-focused workout.

name: Dragon Flag
description: The dragon flag lies on a bench or the floor, grips behind the head and lowers the straight body from a vertical position while keeping the hips and legs in one rigid line. It is one of the hardest core exercises there is; tuck the knees first and straighten them over weeks, controlling every degree of the descent.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: The dumbbell bench press is a mainstay of workout enthusiasts worldwide. It’s a classic move for building a bigger, stronger chest. As such, it’s often placed first in mass-building chest workouts.

name: Dumbbell Bench Pull
description: The dumbbell bench pull lies chest-down on a high bench and rows a bell in each hand from below, pulling them to the underside of the bench. The pad pins the torso so the back does all the work; lower the bells under full control each rep.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
description: The dumbbell biceps curl is a single-joint exercise for building bigger and stronger biceps. Popular among gym goers of all experience levels, this move can be done seated or standing. It is generally performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or higher, as part of the arm-focused portion of a workout.

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
description: The dumbbell walking calf raise is a dynamic exercise targeting the calf muscles of the lower leg, particularly the gastrocnemius muscle. It can be performed for distance or for reps.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
description: The dumbbell deadlift is a movement that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and back muscles. While it can be performed all the way from the ground, in the style of a barbell deadlift, it is more often performed from the top down as a Romanian deadlift. The dumbbell deadlift can be performed in low rep ranges to build posterior strength, or for moderate to high reps to build muscle and endurance.

name: Dumbbell Face Pull
description: The dumbbell face pull hinges forward and pulls two bells high toward the face with the elbows wide, training the rear delts and the external rotators. Keep the torso still and finish with the elbows above the wrists; light weights and strict paths are the point.

name: Dumbbell Farmer's Walk
description: The dumbbell farmer's walk is an exercise with roots in competitive strongman training, but which is also popular in CrossFit and functional training. It can be a challenging finisher to any workout, or work well in fat-loss circuit training or as an accessory movement to heavy lifts like the deadlift.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
description: The dumbbell floor press is a multijoint pressing exercise performed lying on the floor. It can be performed either with the knees bent or flat. The floor press limits the range of motion you would achieve with a regular dumbbell bench press, but still targets the chest, triceps, and anterior delts. This allows you to press more weight than in a dumbbell bench press, and perhaps put less stress on the shoulders.

name: Dumbbell Fly
description: The dumbbell chest fly is a popular exercise that targets the pectoral or chest muscles. It attempts to isolate the chest muscles, stretching and contracting them while limiting involvement of the shoulders. Unlike a press, where the elbows bend and flex, flyes should keep a relatively consistent elbow angle. The motion is sometimes compared to \"hugging a tree.\" Dumbbell flyes are usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a chest or upper-body focused workout.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
description: The dumbbell front raise is a single-joint exercise targeting the shoulder muscles, particularly the front or anterior deltoids. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, at least 8-12 reps per set, as part of an upper-body or shoulder-focused workout.

name: Dumbbell Front Squat
description: The dumbbell front squat is a popular exercise for targeting the muscles of the lower body, including the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. Holding dumbbells in the racked position also works the core and upper-back muscles to maintain posture while the lower body moves. Because the amount of weight you can use will be limited by what you can clean to the rack position, this movement is usually performed for moderate to high reps, at least 8-12 reps per set or more. If this movement hurts your knees, try performing it with a wider stance.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
description: This curl is performed simultaneously with dumbbells but without wrist supination. Throughout each rep, the wrists remain neutral, like a carpenter hammering a nail.

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
description: The dumbbell hip thrust drives the hips to full extension with a bell across the pelvis, a low-friction alternative to the barbell version. Squeeze the glutes at the top and keep the chin tucked; pad the bell on the hip bone for comfort.

name: Dumbbell Kickstand Deadlift
description: The dumbbell kickstand deadlift is a movement targeting the muscles of the hamstrings, glutes, and back. The kickstand position can help focus the stretch and contraction on each individual leg, similar to a single-leg Romanian deadlift, while presenting less of a balance challenge. It can be performed in low reps, such as 5-8 reps per set, for strengthening the posterior chain, or for higher reps for muscle growth.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: The dumbbell lateral raise is a shoulder exercise that targets the medial or middle head of the deltoid muscle. It's a staple strength-training move and is a great option for accessory work on upper-body training days. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, at least 8-12 reps, as part of the upper-body or shoulder-focused portion of a workout.

name: Dumbbell Lunge
description: The dumbbell split squat is a popular lower-body exercise to build strength and muscle one leg at a time. It can be used to teach proper lunge form, but is also valuable on its own when trained in traditional strength-focused rep ranges, such as 5-8 reps per set, or for higher reps to build muscle or for conditioning.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Carry
description: The dumbbell overhead carry walks with one bell locked out overhead, training shoulder stability and anti-side-bend core strength at once. Keep the bell stacked over the shoulder and the hip and the ribs down; switch sides at the halfway point.

name: Dumbbell Pistol Squat
description: The dumbbell pistol squat holds a bell at the chest as counterweight while squatting to a single leg, making the balance point easier to find. Keep the standing heel down and the free leg long; the bell reaches forward as the hips sink back.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
description: The dumbbell pull-over is a popular muscle and strength-building exercise that targets the muscles of the chest, upper back, lats, and the serratus anterior. It was a favorite of old-school bodybuilders, who believed high-rep pull-overs helped build a V-taper shape in the torso.

name: Dumbbell Push Press
description: The dumbbell push press dips the knees slightly and drives two bells overhead with leg power, allowing heavier loads than the strict press. Time the dip and drive as one; the arms only finish the job the legs start.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
description: With the reverse-grip dumbbell curl, the palms face down, not up. This unorthodox wrist position simultaneously targets the biceps while also building forearm and grip strength. The move can be performed standing or seated. Because grip is a limiting factor, it is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-10 reps per set.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
description: The incline dumbbell reverse fly is an upper-body exercise targeting the posterior or rear deltoids, as well as the postural muscles of the upper back. Because it targets such small muscles, this exercise is usually performed with light weight for high reps, such as 10-15 reps per set or more.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
description: The dumbbell reverse wrist curl trains the wrist extensors, hinging the backs of the hands up from a braced forearm position. These muscles tire fast and respond to light, high-rep work; keep the forearms glued down and the movement in the wrists only.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
description: The dumbbell stiff-legged deadlift targets the hamstrings, glutes, low and upper back, as well as the core. The purpose of the stiff-legged, as opposed to Romanian deadlift with slightly bent knees, is to engage the hamstrings and low back to an even greater degree.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: The standing dumbbell shoulder press is a classic deltoid-builder (especially the front deltoids) that’s ubiquitous in gyms around the world. Performing the move standing up as opposed to seated allows for more weight to be used.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
description: The standing dumbbell shrug is a popular movement to build and strengthen the trapezius muscles. It’s a often trained on a bodybuilding-style shoulder or back training day, but can also work well in full-body or strength-focused training.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: The dumbbell side bend is a popular exercise for targeting the oblique muscles of the abdomen. It is usually performed for relatively high reps, at least 8-12 reps per set or more. It can be performed one side at a time or alternating sides.

name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
description: The dumbbell skullcrusher is a triceps exercise that has been a staple of bodybuilders for decades. Skullcrushers are usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of an upper-body or arm-focused workout.

name: Dumbbell Snatch
description: The dumbbell snatch drives a single bell from the floor or the hang to overhead in one explosive pull, catching it locked out with a dip. It is a fast, forgiving full-body power lift; keep the bell close on the way up and punch through at the top.

name: Dumbbell Somersault Squat
description: The dumbbell somersault squat holds a bell at the chest and squats while rolling the torso in a controlled forward circle, keeping constant tension on the quads through an honest range. Move slowly, so the circle feels like a controlled tilt rather than a wobble; the bell's front load keeps the spine tall.

name: Dumbbell Split Squat
description: The dumbbell split squat is a popular lower-body exercise to build strength and muscle one leg at a time. It can be used to teach proper lunge form, but is also valuable on its own when trained in traditional strength-focused rep ranges, such as 5-8 reps per set, or for higher reps to build muscle or for conditioning.

name: Dumbbell Squat
description: The dumbbell squat is a classic lower-body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. While this variation is usually performed with relatively light weights for high reps, it can also be used as a substitute for squats or the trap-bar deadlift in any workout.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
description: The dumbbell sumo squat is a popular lower-body movement using a single dumbbell held in front of the legs. It is performed with a wider than shoulder-width stance, which increases the demand on the glutes, hamstrings, and adductors while still benefiting the quads, core, and upper body. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, at least 8-12 reps per set, as part of the lower-body portion of a workout.

name: Dumbbell Svend Press
description: The dumbbell Svend press presses the top of a bell between both palms out from the chest, an isometric squeeze that lights up the inner pecs. Keep the squeeze relentless through the whole range; short range, high tension, high reps.

name: Dumbbell Tricep Extension
description: The dumbbell tricep extension lowers a bell behind the head from an overhead grip, stretching the triceps' long head through its fullest range. Keep the elbows narrow and pointing forward; the deeper the stretch, the better the rep, within shoulder comfort.

name: Dumbbell Tricep Kickback
description: The single-arm triceps kick-back is an isolation move from a bent-over position used to increase size and strength of the triceps.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
description: The standing dumbbell upright row is a popular movement for building stronger and bigger traps and shoulders. Many lifters combine this move with either their back or shoulder workout, since it involves both body parts. It is generally performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more.

name: Dumbbell Windmill
description: The dumbbell windmill holds a bell overhead and hinges sideways to touch the floor with the free hand, keeping the eyes on the bell throughout. It stretches the hip and hamstring of one side while the shoulder stabilizes a load overhead; move slowly and keep the bell arm vertical.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
description: The dumbbell wrist curl curls the wrists up from a braced forearm position, training the flexors one or two hands at a time. Full range matters more than load; let the bell roll down to the fingertips, then curl it back with the fingers and wrist together.

name: Eagle Pose
description: Eagle pose wraps one leg over the other and binds the arms in front of the chest, holding the tangled balance. It stretches the outer hips and between the shoulder blades while demanding steady single-leg control; swap the wrap direction to even both sides.

name: Easy Pose
description: Easy pose is a simple seated cross-legged position used to settle posture and breathing. Sit tall on the sitting bones, let the knees drop toward the floor and alternate the leg crossing to keep the hips symmetrical.

name: Elliptical Trainer
description: The elliptical trainer is a popular machine for cardiovascular training without the significant impact on your joints of running. On many machines, you can adjust the resistance level to make the movement more difficult for all four limbs. The elliptical is a mainstay in most commercial gyms, and can be equally effective for HIIT-style interval workouts or for longer-duration endurance work.

name: Extended Side Angle Pose
description: Extended side angle pose sinks into a wide lunge and lays the same-side forearm on the thigh, reaching the top arm over the ear to lengthen the whole side body. Keep the chest open toward the ceiling rather than collapsing forward.

name: EZ Bar Pullover
description: The EZ-bar pullover arcs the angled bar from the chest to beyond the head while lying down, stretching the lats and ribcage under load. The angled grip spares the shoulders that a straight bar punishes; keep the hips planted and the arms softly bent.

name: EZ Bar Reverse Grip Row
description: The EZ-bar reverse-grip row rows the bar to the lower ribs with palms up, shifting the pull toward the lats and biceps. Keep the torso hinged close to parallel and the elbows tracking close to the body; squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.

name: EZ Bar Spider Curl
description: The EZ-bar spider curl is an exercise targeting the biceps and performed face down on either an incline bench or on the flat side of a preacher bench. The EZ-bar makes for a more comfortable wrist position, while the angle helps to isolate the biceps and limit involvement of the shoulder muscles. This curl variation is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of upper-body or arm-focused training.

name: EZ-Bar Bench Press
description: The EZ-bar bench press benches with the angled bar, trading a little pec load for a far friendlier wrist and elbow position. Grip the inner bends, keep the forearms vertical at the bottom and drive the bar up in a slight arc over the chest.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
description: The standing EZ-bar curl is an immensely popular exercise targeting the biceps. It is commonly performed for moderate to high reps as part of an upper body or arms-focused workout. Many gyms even have EZ-bars at fixed weights, allowing for easy weight changes.

name: EZ-Bar Front Raise
description: The EZ-bar front raise lifts the angled bar from the thighs to shoulder height, training the front delts with a wrist-friendly grip. Keep the elbows nearly straight and the torso still; raise only to shoulder height, since momentum beyond that is wasted.

name: EZ-Bar Lying Triceps Extension
description: The EZ-bar lying triceps extension lowers the angled bar to the forehead or slightly behind from a locked-out press, isolating the triceps under a deep stretch. Keep the elbows fixed in space pointing at the ceiling; only the forearms travel.

name: EZ-Bar Overhead Tricep Extension
description: The EZ-bar overhead tricep extension lowers the angled bar behind the head from an overhead lockout, stretching the long head of the triceps fully. Keep the elbows narrow and pointing forward, and the ribcage down; the stretch is the working part of the rep.

name: EZ-Bar Reverse Curl
description: The reverse-grip EZ-bar curl is an exercise targeting the biceps and forearms. Because grip strength is a limitation with this move, it is often performed for moderate to high reps as part of an upper-body or arm-focused workout.

name: EZ-Bar Romanian Deadlift
description: The EZ-bar Romanian deadlift hinges the hips back under the angled bar, stretching the hamstrings to their working end and driving back up. The angled grip suits stiff wrists and lets the load sit closer; keep the bar grazing the legs and the spine long.

name: EZ-Bar Shrug
description: The seated EZ-bar shrug is an exercise targeting the trapezius muscle, that V-shaped muscle that forms a triangle where the shoulders meet the neck. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps during an upper-body or shoulders and traps-focused workout.

name: EZ-Bar Upright Row
description: The EZ-bar upright row pulls the angled bar up the front of the body to chest height, working the side delts and traps through a wrist-neutral grip. Keep the elbows above the hands and stop before the pull pinches the shoulder; moderate weight, strict path.

name: EZ-Bar Wrist Curl
