description: The EZ-bar wrist curl flexes the wrists under the angled bar with the forearms braced, training the flexors through the most wrist-comfortable angle available. Full range beats heavy weight here: let the bar roll to the fingertips and curl it back up.

name: Fish Pose
description: Fish pose lies on the back and arches the chest toward the ceiling with the crown of the head resting lightly on the floor. It opens the front of the neck, chest and shoulders after long sitting; keep the weight on the elbows, never on the head.

name: Floor EZ-Bar Press
description: The floor EZ-bar press benches from the floor, which stops the elbows at a safe depth while the angled bar spares the wrists. It hammers the lockout half of the press and the triceps; pause when the upper arms settle before driving up.

name: Floor Kettlebell Pullover
description: The floor kettlebell pullover arcs a bell from the chest to beyond the head and back while lying on the floor, stretching the lats under a light load. The floor keeps the ribs honest; stop the arc if the lower back leaves the ground.

name: Floor Press
description: The floor press presses a barbell from the floor with the shoulder blades pinned, cutting the range at the point the shoulders would take over. It builds raw triceps and lockout strength and spares cranky shoulders; let the triceps rest briefly on the floor between reps.

name: Flutter Kicks
description: The flutter kick is a core exercise where the legs are held off the ground as you flutter your feet over and under each other in small motions. It targets multiple muscles of the core, but particularly the rectus abdominis or \"six-pack\" muscles. It can be performed for time or reps in the ab-focused portion of any workout.

name: Front Lever
description: The front lever hangs from a bar or rings and raises the straight body to horizontal, face-up. It is one of the most demanding straight-arm skills, loading the lats and core enormously; tuck, then advance through one-leg variations before the full hold.

name: Front Squat
description: The front squat squats with the bar racked on the front delts, keeping the torso upright and shifting load toward the quads and upper back. The elbows stay high and the wrists extended; it is the most technically honest of the heavy squats, and a weak position shows immediately.

name: Garland Pose
description: Garland pose settles into a deep squat with the heels down and the elbows pressing the knees outward. It opens the adductors, ankles and hips and is an excellent diagnostic of squat mobility; elevate the heels slightly if they lift.

name: Glute Bridge
description: The glute bridge is a popular lower-body bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the glutes, but also activates the lower back and hamstrings. It can be performed with body weight alone, or with added resistance such as barbells, dumbbells, or bands. It can be performed for time or reps and works perfectly in a dynamic warm-up for lower-body training, but can also be performed for glute activation anytime.

name: Glute Bridge Hold
description: The glute bridge hold lifts the hips into full extension and keeps them there, squeezing the glutes continuously. Push through the heels, tuck the pelvis and stop short of arching the lower back; holds of 20 to 45 seconds build endurance in the posterior chain.

name: Glute Kickback
description: The glute kickback extends one leg straight back and up from a quadruped position, isolating the glute of the working hip. Keep the hips square to the floor, since the leg lifts by squeezing the glute, not by arching the back; small range, hard squeeze.

name: Glute Kickback Hold
description: The glute kickback hold suspends a leg extended behind the body from a quadruped position, holding it against gravity. Keep the hips square to the floor; height matters less than a locked-in pelvis. It is a glute isolation drill rather than a leg lift.

name: Goblet Squat
description: The goblet squat is a popular lower-body exercise where you hold a kettlebell or dumbbell in front of your chest as if you are supporting a heavy cup or goblet. It can help lifters of all levels improve their squat technique and hip mobility, but can also work as a muscle-building or strength accessory movement for experienced athletes. It also works well in combinations, complexes, and flows with other kettlebell movements like swings, presses, and cleans.

name: Good Morning
description: The barbell good morning is an exercise that targets glute, hamstring, and lower back development. It is often trained as an accessory movement to the deadlift, but also has value on its own. It is sometimes performed for reps in traditional strength-focused rep ranges such as 5-8 reps per set, but due to the risk posed to the lower back, is rarely treated as a max-effort single-rep lift.

name: Hack Squat
description: The hack squat is a machine-based exercise that targets the muscles of the legs, particularly the quadriceps. It is often used as an accessory for squats, but can also be the main lower-body movement in a workout. It is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more.

name: Hack Squat Calf Raise
description: The hack squat calf raise is a variation of the standing calf raise performed in a hack squat machine. This allows for heavy loading, but also shoulder comfort from the pads of the hack squat. Calf raise variations are often performed for relatively high reps, such as 10-20 reps per set or more.

name: Half Moon Pose
description: Half moon pose balances on one leg with the torso tipped to horizontal and the free leg lifted to hip height or above. It trains balance and hip stability while opening the standing-side hamstring; a block under the lower hand keeps the spine long.

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Rock
description: The half-kneeling hip flexor rock rocks the hips forward and back from a half-kneeling stance, rhythmically loading and releasing the front of the rear hip. Keep the glute of the rear leg squeezed and the ribs down; it is a controlled mobility drill, not a stretch-and-forget hold.

name: Handstand Push Ups
description: The handstand push-up is an exercise targeting the shoulders, although other muscles assist in the completion of the reps. It is common in both CrossFit workouts and advanced bodyweight or calisthenics training. Given the degree of difficulty, beginners will need to progress to this move.

name: Hang Clean
description: The hang clean pulls the bar from above the knee to the shoulders in one explosive extension, trading the floor pull for pure power from the hang. Keep the bar close as the hips extend, then whip the elbows under into the front rack.

name: Hang Power Clean
description: The hang power clean catches the bar above parallel in a shallow dip, pulling from the hang and landing tall. It is the most repeatable clean variation for power work; the same crisp extension with less demand on the front-rack mobility.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: The alternating hanging knee raise is an exercise targeting the abs, but which also works the lats and hip flexors. Rather than performing both legs at a time, you lift one knee at a time and alternate with each rep as if marching in place. Knee raises are often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or more, as part of ab-focused training.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: The hanging leg raise is an exercise targeting the abs, but which also works the lats and hip flexors. Instead of resting your forearms on the pads of a captain's chair, you perform these hanging from a bar. Experienced lifters make these look easy, but beginners may need time to build up to sets of 8-12 reps.

name: Hanging Pike
description: The hanging pike hangs from a bar and raises the straight legs to hip height or above, piking the hips toward the bar. Keep the swing out of the rep: the hips curl, the legs do not simply swing. It sits between the knee raise and the toes-to-bar.

name: Happy Baby Pose
description: Happy baby pose lies on the back, grips the outsides of the feet and draws the knees toward the armpits. It releases the adductors and lower back gently; rock side to side for a light spinal massage and keep the tailbone heavy on the floor.

name: Head-to-Knee Pose
description: Head-to-knee pose folds one straight leg toward the chest while hinging over the extended other leg. Keep the lengthened spine rather than chasing the shin with a rounded back; it stretches the hamstring and calf of the extended leg.

name: Heel-Elevated Squat
description: The heel-elevated squat raises the heels on a plate or wedge and squats, letting the knees travel further forward to load the quads through a longer range. Keep the torso upright and sink between the feet; the depth the wedge buys is the point.

name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
description: The heel-to-toe walk walks in a straight line placing the heel of one foot directly before the toes of the other, a balance drill that challenges the ankles and the stabilizing chain of the standing leg. Keep the arms at the sides and the gaze ahead, not down.

name: Hero Pose
description: Hero pose kneels between the feet with the calves alongside the thighs, stretching the quads and ankles deeply. Sit on a block if the hips cannot reach the floor and keep the spine upright; short holds are enough at first.

name: Hex Bar Deadlift
description: The hex bar deadlift is a variety of deadlift performed in a hexagonal barbell also known as a trap bar. The bar is held with a parallel (palms in) grip outside of the legs. It is biomechanically different from a barbell deadlift in that it lines up with a lifter’s center of gravity, rather than placing it in front of their body. The trap bar deadlift can be trained in traditional strength and muscle-focused rep range, or for higher reps. It activates all of the same muscle groups as conventional or sumo deadlifts, including the glutes, quads, hamstring, lower back, lats, upper back, and grip.

name: High Knees
description: High knees is a full-body, cardio-based exercise with an emphasis on the lower body. It is often performed for reps or time as part of a dynamic warm-up.

name: High Plank
description: The high plank holds the top of a push-up with straight arms, stacking the shoulders over the wrists and bracing the whole trunk. Push the floor away, squeeze the glutes and keep the neck long; it is both a core drill and the setup for push-up variations.

name: High-Foot Leg Press
description: The high-foot leg press places the feet high and wide on the platform so the hips and hamstrings do most of the pushing. The knees travel less and the glutes load hardest at depth; expect it to feel closer to a hinge than a squat.

name: Hip Adduction
description: The machine hip adduction squeezes the legs together against weighted pads, training the adductors directly. Keep the movement smooth through the full travel; the stretch at the wide position is where most of the value lives.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: The hollow-body hold is an isometric exercise that increases strength and stability in the core muscles. It is common in gymnastics training, CrossFit training, and as a core tension and bracing drill for lifters and athletes of all types. It is performed for time and can be performed as an activation drill prior to lifting, as part of a circuit, or as equipment-free core training anytime.

name: Horizontal Leg Press
description: The horizontal leg press pushes a weighted sled along a rail from a reclined seat, loading the legs without compressing the spine. Keep the whole foot flat and the pelvis on the pad; the range should end before the hips curl off the seat.

name: Human Flag
description: The human flag grips a vertical pole and holds the straight body sideways off it. It demands exceptional oblique and shoulder strength; the progression runs through tucked, straddle and negative versions long before the full flag.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
description: The incline bench press is an upper body compound movement that targets the upper chest.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
description: The incline dumbbell biceps curl is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps. This variation targets the long head of the biceps more than a traditional curl and there is more overall tension to this muscle.

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
description: The incline dumbbell chest fly is an upper body isolation exercise targeting the upper chest and is typically used with aesthetic goals in mind. It will require less weight than an incline press, which makes it a great hypertrophy exercise with high reps.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: The incline dumbbell bench press is an upper body exercise targeting the upper pectoral muscles.

name: Incline EZ-Bar Bench Press
description: The incline EZ-bar bench press presses from an incline bench with the angled bar, biasing the upper chest while easing wrist and elbow strain. Keep the bar path over the collar line, the elbows about 45 degrees from the torso and the shoulder blades pinched.

name: Incline Hammer Curl
description: The incline hammer curl curls from an incline bench with the arms hanging behind the torso, putting the biceps under a long stretch while the neutral grip targets the brachialis. Keep the elbows still and let the arm hang fully at the bottom; the stretch is the growth zone.

name: Incline Push-Up
description: The hands-elevated push-up is a variation on the push-up, a body-weight standard. The hands are elevated, so that your body is aligned at an angle to the floor rather than parallel.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
description: The incline treadmill walk sets the belt to a steep grade and walks at a steady pace, turning a low-impact stroll into a demanding conditioning tool. The glutes and calves do much of the work; resist the urge to grip the handrails, which unloads the legs.

name: Inverted Row
description: The Smith machine inverted row is a bodyweight exercise targeting the muscles of the lats (latissimus dorsi) and upper back, using the bar of the Smith machine to hang and pull from. You can change the bar height to customize the difficulty level and desired angle of the row. This variation is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more.

name: Isometric Neck Lateral Flexion
description: Isometric neck lateral flexion presses the hand against the side of the head while the neck resists sideways bending. Train both sides evenly and keep the pressure modest; steady holds build the neck strength that contact sports and heavy pulls demand.

name: Jackknife Sit-Up
description: The jackknife sit-up raises the straight arms and legs together from the floor until the hands meet the shins overhead, folding the body in two. Keep the lower back on the floor and hinge at the hips while the ribs curl up; lower both ends slowly.

name: Jefferson Curl
description: The Jefferson curl rolls the spine down one vertebra at a time while holding a light weight, then unrolls back to standing, loading the entire back line through flexion and extension. Start nearly unloaded and move with extreme control; it is a mobility-strength drill for the spine and hamstrings, not a heavy lift.

name: Jump Rope
description: Jump rope turns a rope over the head and under the feet in continuous small hops, training the calves, shoulders and coordination while spiking the heart rate. Stay on the balls of the feet with low, quiet bounces; it scales from easy warm-up rounds to brutal intervals.

name: Jump Squat
description: The jump squat is an explosive bodyweight exercise targeting the quads, hamstrings, and glutes. It is also a serious cardiovascular challenge when done for reps. It can be performed as a power exercise to build jumping power, or in any fat-loss or athleticism-focused workout.

name: Jumping Jacks
description: The jumping jack is a classic calisthenics exercise to improve overall conditioning. It’s one the most recognizable exercises on the planet, and it’s almost synonymous with training for military recruits. It can be done for time or reps, often in dynamic warm-ups or to mobilize the hips and shoulders.

name: Kettlebell Bulgarian Split Squat
description: The kettlebell Bulgarian split squat loads a rear-foot-elevated split squat with one or two bells held at the chest or at the sides. The kettlebell's pull keeps the torso honest; sink the back knee and drive up through the front heel.

name: Kettlebell Close-Grip Floor Press
description: The kettlebell close-grip floor press lies on the floor and presses two bells with the elbows tucked close to the ribs. The floor stops the elbow safely and the narrow path loads the triceps hard; pause when the upper arms settle before the next rep.

name: Kettlebell Concentration Curl
description: The kettlebell concentration curl braces the working elbow against the inner thigh and curls a bell in strict isolation. The brace removes every shortcut; squeeze at the top and lower slowly under control.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
description: The kettlebell deadlift is a foundational movement in kettlebell training. It's often taught as a buildup or regression to the kettlebell swing, as well as to instruct the \"hip hinge\" motion in a more approachable manner than with a barbell.

name: Kettlebell Farmer's Walk
description: The kettlebell farmer's walk carries a heavy bell in each hand for distance or time. The grip, traps and core hold everything together while the legs walk; stay tall, keep the shoulders packed and take short, quick steps.

name: Kettlebell Floor Press
description: The kettlebell alternating floor press limits the range of motion you would achieve with a dumbbell or kettlebell bench press, but still targets the chest, triceps, and anterior delts. This allows you to build strength in the top portion of the lift, overload the triceps, and work on strengthening the shoulder stabilizers.

name: Kettlebell Goblet Lunge
description: The kettlebell goblet lunge holds a bell at the chest through lunges, front-loading the torso so the core works as hard as the legs. The counterweight makes it easy to keep the spine tall; step or walk, and keep the front knee tracking over the shoe.

name: Kettlebell Halo
description: The kettlebell halo circles a bell around the head at collarbone height, training shoulder mobility and core control. Keep the hips quiet, since the movement belongs to the shoulders and ribs; reverse directions halfway through each set.

name: Kettlebell Hammer Curl
description: The kettlebell hammer curl curls the bell by its handle with the wrist neutral, biasing the brachialis and forearm. Keep the elbow pinned to the side and let the bell rotate naturally in the hand.

name: Kettlebell Hip Thrust
description: The kettlebell hip thrust drives the hips to full extension with a bell padded across the pelvis. The single-bell setup needs no bar or bench changes; squeeze the glutes hard at the top and keep the chin tucked.

name: Kettlebell Kickstand Deadlift
description: The kettlebell kickstand deadlift hinges with one foot's toe kicked back behind the other, splitting the difference between a bilateral and a single-leg pattern. The rear leg is a kickstand, not a worker; keep the weight over the front leg and push the hips back.

name: Kettlebell Lunge Press
description: The kettlebell lunge press steps into a lunge and presses the bell overhead as the knee descends. The legs create instability that the pressing shoulder must absorb; alternate legs and keep the wrist stacked over the elbow.

name: Kettlebell Offset Reverse Lunge and Press
description: The kettlebell offset reverse lunge and press holds the bell on one side while stepping back and pressing it up, forcing the core to fight the off-center load through the whole rep. Keep the torso square to the front; the offset is the point.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Carry
description: The kettlebell overhead carry walks with a bell locked out overhead, training shoulder stability, core strength and grip in one drill. Keep the bicep near the ear and the ribcage stacked over the pelvis; switch hands at the halfway mark.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Tricep Extension
description: The kettlebell overhead tricep extension lowers a bell behind the head from a locked-out overhead grip and presses it back up. Keep the elbows pointing forward and the ribs down; the stretch at the bottom is the growth position.

name: Kettlebell Pistol Squat
description: The kettlebell pistol squat holds a bell at the chest as counterweight while squatting on one leg. The weight shifts the balance point backward, making the hardest part of the pistol, staying over the foot, far more manageable.

name: Kettlebell Pullover
description: The kettlebell pullover arcs a bell from the chest to behind the head and back while lying down, stretching the lats and demanding core control. Keep the lower back pinned to the floor; the moment it arches, the weight is too heavy.

name: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge
description: The kettlebell reverse lunge steps back under load held at the chest or in the rack, sparing the knees while loading the quads and glutes. Keep the torso upright and let the front leg own the depth; the bell counterbalances the hinge.

name: Kettlebell Reverse Wrist Curl
description: The kettlebell reverse wrist curl trains the wrist extensors, resting the forearms on the thighs and letting the backs of the hands hinge the bell up. Light weight and high control; the extensors respond to volume, not grinding singles.

name: Kettlebell Rotational Lunge
description: The kettlebell rotational lunge sweeps the bell across the body into a lunge, blending a lateral step, a rotation and a squat. Let the hips lead the turn and keep the arms relatively long; it is a favorite athletic warm-up and conditioner.

name: Kettlebell Russian Twist
description: The kettlebell Russian twist sits with the heels down and sweeps the bell side to side across the floor, rotating through the ribcage. Keep the chest tall rather than slumping; the harder the rotation, the less the arms should lead.

name: Kettlebell Shrug
description: The kettlebell shrug lifts the shoulders straight toward the ears against heavy bells, training the upper traps. Keep the arms long and the elbows soft; a one-second hold at the top beats momentum.

name: Kettlebell Single Leg Deadlift
description: The kettlebell single-leg deadlift is a variation on the kettlebell deadlift where one foot stays planted on the ground while the other raises into the air at the bottom of the movement. It's popular in lower-body training for strength and muscle building, but also trains balance, grip, and the core muscles.

name: Kettlebell Skull Crusher
description: The kettlebell skull crusher lowers the bells beside the head from a locked-out press and extends back up, isolating the triceps. The bell's center of mass pulls the hands slightly apart, which many elbows prefer over a straight bar.

name: Kettlebell Squat
description: The kettlebell squat holds the bell at the chest through a full squat, front-loading the body so the core and upper back work with the legs. Keep the elbows inside the knees at the bottom and the chest proud throughout.

name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift
description: The kettlebell sumo deadlift pulls a heavy bell from between the feet in a wide stance, training the glutes, adductors and grip through a full hinge. Wedge the hips down to the bell, keep the shins vertical and stand tall by driving the floor away.

name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
description: The kettlebell sumo deadlift high pull is a dynamic kettlebell exercise that focuses on the muscles of the posterior chain, including the hamstrings, glutes, traps, rear delts, and upper back. It can be done in lower reps for power or strength, or higher reps for conditioning and fat loss. It can also be a component of a circuit-style kettlebell workout, either for time or reps.

name: Kettlebell Svend Press
description: The kettlebell Svend press squeezes a bell flat between the palms and presses it straight out at chest height. The isometric squeeze is the exercise: the pecs work to hold the bell while the press adds range. Keep the elbows soft.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: The kettlebell swing is a popular lower-body exercise emphasizing the hamstrings, glutes, and back muscles. It is often used to train explosive power, for aerobic or cardiovascular conditioning, in circuit training, or as an accessory movement for the deadlift.

name: Kettlebell Swing Clean
description: The kettlebell swing clean catches a swing-height bell into the rack position without the extra vertical of a full clean. It teaches the punch-through that all clean work relies on; let the hips throw the bell and the hand merely steers it.

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Ups
description: The kettlebell Turkish get up travels from lying on the back to standing with a bell locked out overhead, through a sequence of deliberate positions. It is equal parts shoulder stability, hip strength and total-body control; move slowly enough that every step could be paused.

name: Kettlebell Windmills
description: The single-kettlebell windmill is a dynamic kettlebell exercise emphasizing core strength and shoulder and hip mobility and stability. It is often used as a functional warm-up or for multi-directional strength work. It doesn't work as well in a metcon or conditioning setting, and shouldn't be performed under intense fatigue.

name: Kettlebell Wrist Curl
description: The kettlebell wrist curl rests the forearms on the thighs and hinges the bell up with the fingers flexed, training the wrist flexors and grip. Use a light bell and a full range; the hands tolerate high reps here better than heavy grinds.

name: Knee Push Ups
description: The knee push up performs the push-up with the knees on the floor, cutting the load roughly in half while keeping the pressing pattern intact. Keep a straight line from the shoulders to the knees with no sagging hips; it is the standard on-ramp to full push ups.

name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
description: The knee-to-chest stretch lies on the back and draws one or both knees in toward the chest. It decompresses the lower back and releases the glutes; keep the head relaxed on the floor and breathe into the stretch.

name: Kneeling Cable Row
description: The kneeling cable row kneels facing a low pulley and rows the handle to the ribs, forcing the core to hold the torso upright without a bench or seat. Keep the hips square and the pull strong through the elbow; the kneeling stance quietly doubles as a hip-flexor stretch.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
description: The kneeling hip flexor stretch is a stretch targeting greater flexibility in the front side of the hips. It targets a chronically tight muscle group and is often performed as part of a dynamic warm-up, a cool-down, or as recovery work after training.

name: Kneeling Wrist Stretch
description: The kneeling wrist stretch kneels and places the backs of the hands on the floor with fingers toward the knees, leaning gently to extend the wrists. It is a favorite of lifters and climbers; ease off if any position produces sharp pain.

name: L Sit
description: The L sit holds the straight legs out in front of the body while supported on the hands, on the floor or on parallel bars. It builds tremendous hip-flexor and triceps strength and core control; start with one leg tucked or brief 5-second holds.

name: Landmine Press
description: The landmine press presses the end of a barbell set in a landmine attachment or corner up and forward from the shoulder. The angled path spares the shoulder joint while still loading the delts and chest; step into it and drive through the front foot.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: The lat pull-down is a cable-based exercise that's ubiquitous in gyms around the world. This back builder is easy to learn and highly effective at building back size and strength. It's usually trained in moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set. If grip strength is a limitation, you can wear wrist straps.

name: Leg Extension
description: The leg extension is an isolation exercise for the quads.

name: Leg Press
description: The leg press is a machine exercise targeting the quadriceps. It’s favorite among lifters who prefer the seated position to standing with a load on the spine.

name: Legs-Up-the-Wall Pose
description: Legs-up-the-wall pose rests the legs vertically against a wall while the back lies on the floor. It drains fatigue from the legs, relaxes the hamstrings and lower back, and is a classic recovery posture after hard training days.

name: Lizard Stretch
description: The lizard stretch drops into a deep low lunge with both hands inside the front foot, sinking the hips toward the floor. It opens the hip flexors and adductors at once; forearms down or the back knee lifted both work, whichever keeps the front knee tracking out.

name: Locust Pose
description: Locust pose lies face-down and lifts the chest, arms and legs against gravity, strengthening the entire back side of the body. Keep the lift modest and the neck neutral; it is one of the safest ways to build spinal-erector endurance.

name: Low Lunge
description: The low lunge rests the back knee on the floor in a long split stance, opening the hip flexors of the trailing leg. Keep the torso tall and tuck the pelvis before deepening; adding a gentle side bend or reach multiplies the stretch.

name: Low Lunge to Half Split
description: This flow rocks from a low lunge into a half split and back, alternating a hip-flexor stretch with a hamstring stretch in one continuous movement. Move slowly with the breath; it is a highly efficient warm-up for running, squatting and kicking patterns.

name: Lunge
description: The lunge steps forward or backward into a split stance and sinks until both knees approach right angles, training the legs one side at a time. Keep the front knee over the shoe and the torso tall; alternate legs or complete one side first, both are fine.

name: Lying Leg Curl
description: The lying leg curl is a popular machine-based exercise for the legs, particularly the hamstrings. It is similar to the seated leg curl, but the open hip angle in the lying leg curl may incorporate more glute and calf activation. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a leg pre-exhaust or as a muscle-building movement for lower-body training.

name: Lying Leg Raise
description: The alternating lying leg lift is a popular bodyweight exercise targeting the muscles of the abs, the rectus abdominis or “six-pack” muscles in particular. It can be performed for time or reps in the core-focused portion of any workout.

name: Lying Tricep Extension
description: The lying cable triceps extension is an isolation exercise performed lying on either a bench or the floor. This movement is usually performed for moderate to high reps for a burn and pump as part of an arm-focused workout.

name: Machine Assisted Dips
description: The machine assisted dip kneels or stands on the counterweight platform of an assisted dip station and performs dips with part of the bodyweight removed. Set the assist as low as honest reps allow; the movement pattern and elbow position stay identical to the free-weight dip, which makes it the standard bridge toward full dips.

name: Machine Back Extension
description: The machine back extension trains the spinal erectors through a controlled hinge and raise against a weight stack. Hinge from the hips, keep the ribs down and squeeze the glutes to finish; the movement should come from the hips, not a whip of the lower back.

name: Machine Bicep Curl
description: The machine bicep curl locks the elbows into a pad and moves the handle through a fixed arc, isolating the biceps. The pad removes all swing; let the arm fully straighten at the bottom and squeeze at the top of each rep.

name: Machine Calf Raise
description: The machine seated calf raise is an exercise targeting the calf muscles of the lower leg, particularly the soleus muscle. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set, and occasionally for very high burnout-focused sets of 50-100 total reps.

name: Machine Chest Fly
description: The machine chest fly is a machine-based exercise targeting the chest. It approximates the motion of a dumbbell fly or cable fly, but is usually performed facing forward and seated upright. The motion is often compared to bear-hugging a tree trunk. The chest fly is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a pre-exhaust or muscle-building upper-body workout.

name: Machine Chest Press
description: The machine chest press is a machine-based exercise targeting the chest. It approximates the motion of a bench press but is usually performed facing forward and seated upright. Many machines offer multiple grip options, such as overhand, neutral (palms facing), or underhand. The chest press is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a pre-exhaust or muscle-building upper-body workout.

name: Machine Hip Abduction
description: The machine hip abduction pushes the legs apart against a weighted pad, isolating the glute medius and upper glutes. Sit tall with the chest up and control the return; a slight forward lean changes the feel but should be deliberate, not a slump.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
description: The machine preacher curl is a popular exercise to build size and strength in the biceps. It approximates the motion of a free-weight preacher curl, but uses a selectorized weight stack or plate-loaded machine. Many such machines offer different grips and grip widths. Machine biceps curls are often done for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of the upper-body or arm-focused portion of a workout.

name: Machine Seated Crunch
description: The machine seated crunch loads a crunch through a padded lever, letting the abdominals train against a measurable stack. Curl the ribs toward the pelvis and exhale hard at the top; the weight should move because the trunk rounds, not because the arms pull.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
description: The machine shoulder press is a machine-based exercise targeting the deltoid muscles. It approximates the motion of a free-weight shoulder press, but uses a selectorized weight-stack or plate-loaded machine. Many such machines also allow you to choose between different grips and grip widths. Machine shoulder presses are often done for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of the upper-body or shoulder-focused portion of a workout.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
description: The machine triceps extension is an isolation exercise targeting the tricep muscles.

name: Medicine Ball Slam
description: The medicine ball slam is an explosive exercise for developing power, strength, and speed. Muscles worked include the abdominals, legs, triceps, shoulders, and lats. The slams are usually done in rapid succession to complete one set. It can also be a component of a power or athleticism-focused circuit workout.

name: Mountain Climbers
description: The mountain climber is a popular bodyweight exercise targeting the muscles of the core, as well as the shoulders, hips, and cardiovascular system. It involves lifting one knee to the chest at a time from a straight-arm plank position. It can be performed for time or reps as part of a dynamic warm-up, for bodyweight cardio or conditioning, or as no-equipment dynamic core training.

name: Mountain Pose
description: Mountain pose is standing tall with the weight balanced evenly across both feet and the crown of the head reaching up. It looks like nothing, but it trains the posture, breath and alignment that every other exercise inherits; scan the body from the ground up.

name: Muscle Snatch
description: The muscle snatch pulls the bar overhead without any rebend of the knees or elbows, keeping the arms straight through the finish. It is a strength and position drill for the snatch; go lighter than a power snatch and punch the bar up, then lock it hard.

name: Muscle Ups
description: The muscle up pulls from a hang all the way to support above the bar or rings, blending a high pull with a transition and a dip. It demands pulling power, a false grip or a strong kip and patient technique work; progress through high pulls and chest-to-bar reps first.

name: Neck Side Stretch
description: The neck side stretch tilts the ear toward the shoulder, optionally assisting with a light hand. Keep the opposite shoulder heavy and relaxed; 20 to 30 seconds per side releases the upper trapezius after desk time or heavy carries.

name: Negative Pull Ups
description: The negative pull-up is a multijoint bodyweight exercise that focuses on just one half of the traditional pull-up: the lowering, eccentric, or \"negative\" portion. Because muscles are stronger eccentrically than they are concentrically, many people can perform negatives even if they can't perform full pull-ups. For this reason, it is a popular training tool to help people earn their first pull-up rep, or as a back-off exercise after doing full pull-ups.

name: Neutral Grip Pull Ups
description: The neutral-grip pull-up is a multijoint bodyweight exercise in which the reps are performed with the palms facing one another. Like other pull-up variations, it builds strength and muscle in the upper back, biceps, and core. It can be used as a more shoulder-friendly alternative to straight-bar pull-ups, or to help perform more reps than you can perform overhand.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: The Nordic hamstring curl anchors the ankles and lowers the body forward from the knees with straight hips, fighting the fall with the hamstrings alone. It is one of the most effective hamstring-strength and injury-prevention drills in sport; control the descent and push back up only as far as strength allows.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Bicep Curl
description: The one-arm kettlebell bicep curl curls a single bell with the free hand free, letting the trunk stay honest and adding an anti-rotation demand. Keep the elbow fixed at the side; the bell's offset handle keeps the wrist neutral.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Floor Glute Bridge Press
description: The one-arm kettlebell floor glute bridge press bridges the hips up and presses a bell overhead from the floor at the same time. The bridge locks the pelvis while the shoulder works independently; it builds glute strength and overhead stability in one drill.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
description: The one-arm kettlebell floor press presses a bell from the floor with the shoulder blade pinned, limiting the range safely and hammering the triceps and chest. The floor spots every rep, so heavy singles are fair game; keep the working elbow at about 45 degrees.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Front Squat
description: The one-arm kettlebell front squat squats with a single bell racked, demanding enormous anti-rotation strength from the trunk. The obliques on the unloaded side work as hard as the legs; keep the ribs from flaring toward the bell.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Push Press
description: The one-arm kettlebell push press dips the legs slightly and punches a racked bell overhead, borrowing leg drive to move heavier loads than the strict press. Time the dip and drive together; the arm finishes what the hips start.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Row
description: The one-arm kettlebell row rows a single bell to the hip from a hinged stance, loading the lat while the trunk resists rotation. Keep the shoulders square to the floor and pull the elbow past the ribs; the free hand can brace on the thigh.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Shoulder Press
description: The one-arm kettlebell shoulder press presses a racked bell strictly overhead, training each shoulder and the anti-side-bend core separately. Keep the forearm vertical under the bell and the ribcage stacked over the pelvis; equal sets per side.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Swing
description: The one-arm kettlebell swing swings a single bell between the legs and to chest height, adding anti-rotation work for the trunk and a grip challenge for the hand. Hike the bell back like a football snap and let the hip snap do the throwing; switch hands at the top or between sets.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Push Press
description: The one-arm dumbbell push press drives a single bell overhead with a leg dip and punch, letting one shoulder handle heavier loads while the core resists the sideways lean. Keep the torso square to the front; the dip is small and the drive is violent.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Swing
description: The one-arm dumbbell swing swings a single bell between the legs to shoulder height with a powerful hip snap, the dumbbell cousin of the kettlebell swing. Keep the arm long and let the hips do the throwing; hike the bell back before every rep.

name: One-Arm Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
description: The one-arm kettlebell bottoms-up press presses a bell held upside down by its handle, demanding relentless wrist and shoulder stability. Go far lighter than a normal press; the bell should wobble no more than a few degrees on the way up.

name: One-Arm Kettlebell Tricep Kickback
description: The one-arm kettlebell tricep kickback hinges forward and extends a bent elbow back to lockout, isolating the triceps. Keep the upper arm parallel to the floor and still; only the forearm moves, and the bell's balance demands a steady wrist.

name: One-Arm Landmine Press
description: The one-arm landmine press presses the angled bar with a single arm from the shoulder, training each side while the core resists the twist. The landmine's path lets the shoulder blade move freely; stand staggered and press up and forward along the bar's line.

name: One-Arm Lat Pulldown
description: The one-arm lat pulldown pulls a single handle down beside the body, letting each lat work through its own range without the stronger side covering. Keep the torso square and reach tall at the top; the stretch under load is the best part of the rep.

name: One-Arm Single-Leg Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
description: The single-leg dumbbell Romanian deadlift is a movement targeting the muscles of the hamstrings, glutes, and back. The difference between a Romanian deadlift and a stiff-legged deadlift is the amount of knee bend. The knees are only slightly bent in a stiff-legged deadlift, while they bend more in a Romanian deadlift. Single-leg deadlifts are generally performed for low to moderate reps, such as 8-10 reps per set, with a focus on maximizing the hamstring stretch rather than moving heavy weight. If balance is a challenge, this movement is still very effective if performed while holding on to a stable object for support.

name: One-Arm Single-Leg Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
description: The one-arm single-leg kettlebell Romanian deadlift hinges on one leg while holding the bell in the opposite hand, stacking rotation onto balance. Keep the hips square to the floor, since the temptation to open up is the drill; move slowly and touch nothing.

name: Overhead Squat
description: The overhead squat squats with a bar locked out overhead, demanding mobility, stability and strength from ankles to shoulders at once. It is the deepest test of squat mechanics in the gym; keep the bar over the mid-foot throughout and treat light weights as technique work.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
description: The band overhead triceps extension is a single-joint exercise focused on the triceps that uses the dynamic resistance of the band. The overhead position of the arms targets the long head of the triceps. Many lifters save this move for last in their triceps workout, performing it for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps or more per set.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
description: The overhead triceps stretch reaches one arm overhead and bends the elbow so the hand drops between the shoulder blades, then assists with the opposite hand. Keep the ribs down, since arching the back fakes range; it is the go-to reset after pressing or locking out overhead.

name: Pause Deadlift
description: The pause deadlift stops the pull below the knee for a full breath before finishing, killing momentum and exposing weak positions. Keep the lats engaged and the hips high through the pause; the restart must come from the legs, not a yank.

name: Pause Pull-Up
description: The pause pull up holds the chin over the bar, or the chest at it, for two to three seconds before lowering, building strength through the top range where most pull ups stall. Keep the shoulders down and the body quiet through the hold; no half-rep at the end.

name: Pause Squat
description: The pause squat sits in the hole for two to three seconds before driving up, removing the stretch reflex and forcing pure strength out of the bottom. Stay tight and keep the brace during the pause; the first inch of the ascent is where the rep is won.

name: Paused Bench Press
description: The paused bench press holds the bar dead on the chest for a beat before pressing, killing the bounce and building strength from a dead stop. Keep the shoulder blades pinched and the torso tight through the pause; touch, hold, then drive.

name: Paused Incline Bench Press
description: The paused incline bench press holds the bar dead on the upper chest from an incline bench before pressing, removing momentum from the hardest pressing angle. Keep the wrists stacked and the pause quiet, with no sinking into the rep.

name: Paused Overhead Press
description: The paused overhead press holds the bar at chin or forehead height before pressing to lockout, eliminating the leg-drive bounce and building strength through the sticking point. Keep the torso braced and the bar path straight through the pause.

name: Pec Deck
description: The pec deck is a machine-based exercise targeting the chest. It approximates the motion of a dumbbell fly or cable fly, but is usually performed facing forward and seated upright. The motion is often compared to bear-hugging a tree trunk. The chest fly is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a pre-exhaust or muscle-building upper-body workout.

name: Pendlay Row
description: The Pendlay row, named after the well-known strength coach Glenn Pendlay, is a bent-over row variation where each rep starts with the barbell resting on the ground. This eliminates the stretch reflex and forces the lifter to pull with power and a bent-over spine. The Pendlay row can be performed heavy for low reps, but is usually performed for moderate reps, such as 5-8 per set.

name: Pigeon Stretch
description: The pigeon stretch is a lower-body stretch targeting the glutes, hips, and piriformis. It is similar to the pigeon pose from yoga, but is also popular as part of dynamic warm-ups or cool-downs in strength training. It can also be performed anytime to help combat training-related soreness.

name: Pike Push Ups
description: The pike push up lowers the head toward the floor from a downward-dog position, pressing the body back up with the shoulders overhead. It is the bodyweight bridge toward handstand push ups; keep the hips high and the elbows tracking about 45 degrees back.

name: Pilates Kneeling Side Kick
description: The Pilates kneeling side kick kneels tall and sweeps the top leg forward and back in a controlled arc, training the hip stabilizers and the obliques that keep the torso upright. The trunk does not sway; the leg moves and the body stays. Reach long in both directions.

name: Pilates Leg Pull Back
description: The Pilates leg pull back holds a reverse plank position and lifts one leg at a time, challenging the posterior chain and the shoulder stabilizers together. Keep the hips level as the leg lifts; the trunk is a plank and the leg is punctuation.

name: Pilates Leg Pull Front
description: The Pilates leg pull front holds a high plank and lifts one straight leg slightly off the floor, adding a hip-extension challenge to the anti-rotation plank. Keep the hips square and the shoulders steady; the leg lift is small by design.

name: Pilates Roll Down
description: The Pilates roll down peels the spine off the floor one vertebra at a time and returns the same way, articulating the entire column. Move slowly enough that each segment gets its moment; it teaches segmental control that carries into every hinge and squat.

name: Pilates Roll Over
description: The Pilates roll over lies on the back and rolls the legs overhead until the toes reach beyond the head, articulating the spine one vertebra at a time. Keep the legs straight and the movement slow; it demands control more than flexibility and deserves a warmed-up spine.

name: Pilates Saw
description: The Pilates saw sits with the legs wide and rotates the torso over one leg, reaching the opposite hand past the little toe. Keep the sitting bones planted and rotate from the waist rather than collapsing; it combines spinal rotation with a hamstring stretch.

name: Pilates Side Bend
description: The Pilates side bend holds a side plank on one hand and arcs the top arm overhead, lifting the hips into a long side curve. It trains the obliques and shoulder stabilizers through full range; keep the body in one plane with no twisting toward the floor.

name: Pilates Spine Stretch Forward
description: The Pilates spine stretch forward sits tall with the legs extended and curls the spine forward over the thighs one segment at a time. Reach long rather than round hard; it lengthens the back line of the body while reinforcing deep-core engagement.

name: Pilates Spine Twist
description: The Pilates spine twist rotates the upright torso from side to side on a tall, still lower body. The pelvis stays perfectly level and only the ribs and head turn; it sharpens rotational control that transfers to throws, swings and punches.

name: Pistol Squat
description: The pistol squat descends on a single leg with the other extended straight ahead, the most demanding bodyweight squat there is. Keep the heel down, the shin forward and the hips square; box, heel-elevated and counterweight versions bridge the gap.

name: Planche
description: The planche supports the entire body horizontally on the hands with straight arms and no contact but the palms. It is a years-long skill progression loading the shoulders, wrists and core beyond almost any other bodyweight hold; lean progressively and train tucked versions first.

name: Plank
description: The elbow plank is a popular isometric abdominal exercise. It is common in all types of exercise programs, as well as in group fitness and yoga classes. It targets the muscles of the core, the deep core or transversus abdominis in particular. It is also often prescribed for time to help back pain or to teach proper bracing.

name: Plate Pinch
description: The plate pinch holds one or more weight plates between a straight thumb and fingers at the side. It is a pure grip-strength tool that hits the thumb side of the hand that most other grip work misses; 20 to 45 second holds with both hands work well.

name: Plate Pullover
description: The plate pullover lies on a bench and arcs a weight plate from over the chest to behind the head and back, keeping the arms nearly straight. It stretches the lats and chest under load while training the core to keep the ribs down.

name: Plate-Loaded Donkey Calf Raise
description: The plate-loaded donkey calf raise bends the torso forward and drives the heels up against a pad on the lower back, putting the calves under a long, heavy stretch. Let the heels sink deep at the bottom and pause at the top; the donkey angle places tension on the soleus and gastrocnemius alike.

name: Plate-Loaded Glute Drive
description: The plate-loaded glute drive is a hip thrust machine: the back pads against a bench-style support while the feet drive the platform up through hip extension. The machine handles setup and stability so the glutes can be loaded progressively and heavily.

name: Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise
description: The plate-loaded lateral raise isolates the side delts through a machine's fixed arc with lever arms or a loaded plate. The track removes momentum from the equation; raise to shoulder height and control the descent rather than swinging.

name: Plate-Loaded Shrug
description: The plate-loaded shrug traps the shoulders against a machine's padded levers so the traps lift a heavy load straight up. Shrug up and back, pause briefly at the top, and let the arms stay long; the traps, not the biceps, move the weight.

name: Plow Pose
description: Plow pose rolls the legs overhead until the toes touch the floor behind the head, stretching the entire back line of the body. Support the back with the hands and keep the weight off the neck; roll out slowly and avoid it with any cervical discomfort.

name: Plyo Lunge
description: The plyo lunge jumps to switch the legs mid-air and lands back in a lunge, repeating explosively. Land soft with the hips back and the front knee tracking over the shoe; it builds lower-body power and raises the heart rate fast.

name: Plyo Push-Up
description: The plyo push-up is a bodyweight exercise aimed at increasing upper-body power and strength. It targets the muscles of the chest, triceps, and shoulders, and can be trained in low reps for power and strength, or higher reps for conditioning.

name: Preacher Curl
description: The EZ-bar preacher curl is a classic exercise for building bigger biceps. This move is all about isolation. With the back of the upper arms against the pad, it’s next to impossible to cheat. Go light, get a great pump, and build that peak!

name: Preacher Hammer Curl
description: The preacher hammer curl curls a bell with a neutral grip over a preacher pad, which fixes the elbow and puts the brachialis and forearm under strict tension. Let the arm straighten fully at the bottom of the pad's angle; the stretch there is the point of the exercise.

name: Pseudo Planche Push Ups
description: The pseudo planche push up shifts the hands down beside the hips and leans the shoulders well past the wrists, loading the front delts and straight-arm strength toward the planche. Keep the body hollow and the lean honest; the more forward the shoulders, the harder the rep.

name: Pull-Up
description: The pull-up is a multijoint bodyweight exercise that builds strength and muscle in the upper back, biceps, and core. It is often used as a measurement tool in military or tactical fitness tests, and is an excellent gauge of \"relative strength\" which is strength in relation to body weight.

name: Puppy Pose
description: Puppy pose kneels with the hips over the knees and walks the hands forward, melting the chest toward the floor. It opens the lats, chest and thoracic spine while sparing the lower back; rest the forehead on the ground and breathe into the upper back.

name: Push Jerk
description: The push-jerk is a movement in which the barbell is pushed from the front rack position to overhead with help from the legs. It differs from the push-press in that the lifter dips under the bar rather than simply pushing it up. It is popular in CrossFit workouts and Olympic weightlifting, as well as power training for athletics. It is usually performed for low reps, focusing on power and movement quality.

name: Push Press
description: The push-press is an overhead press variation in which the barbell is pushed upward with assistance from the lower body. This \"push\" helps the weight travel through the sticking point of a strict press. The push-press is commonly performed as part of barbell complexes, power training for all types of athletics, or as a powerful shoulder exercise.

name: Push-Up
description: The push-up is a popular bodyweight exercise that is commonly used in military and tactical physical fitness tests. It’s a classic movement to build upper-body muscle and strength, emphasizing the chest, triceps, and shoulders, but also working the upper back and core.

name: Pyramid Pose
description: Pyramid pose stands in a short forward split with both legs straight and folds the torso over the front leg. It delivers a clean hamstring and calf stretch; square the hips to the front foot and hinge at the hip crease, not the waist.

name: Rack Pull
description: The rack pull is a variation of the deadlift performed from an elevated height, either using boxes, safety pins, or the safeties in a squat rack. It targets all the same muscles as the deadlift, including the glutes, hamstrings, upper back, lower back, and grip. It can be used to strengthen deadlift lockout, but also as a deadlift alternative for people who can't deadlift from the floor without pain.

name: Rear Delt Fly
description: The seated rear delt fly is an upper-body exercise that targets the real deltoid of the shoulder. By performing the movement seated, it eliminates momentum from the rest of the body. This movement is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of the upper-body or shoulder-focused portion of a workout.

name: Reverse Crunches
description: The reverse crunch is a popular exercise targeting the abdominals, particularly the lower half. It’s easy to perform on either the floor or a flat bench. Many lifters think of this as a companion to the crunch, which targets the upper abdominals more than the lower.

name: Reverse Curl
description: The reverse curl curls a barbell with the palms facing down, shifting the work from the biceps to the brachialis and forearm extensors. Keep the elbows pinned and the wrists straight, since curling with bent wrists cheats the forearms out of the rep.

name: Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
description: The reverse-grip bent-over row is a compound exercise used to build strength and size in both the lower and upper back. It targets nearly all of the muscles in the back, but particularly the lats, rhomboids, and lower back. It is thought to target the biceps and lats a bit more directly than overhand barbell rows. Because it can be loaded heavily, it is a popular movement in strength and muscle-focused upper-body workouts.

name: Reverse Grip Lat Pulldown
description: The reverse-grip lat pull-down is variation on the lat pull-down that targets the lower lats more than an overhand grip. Because the hands are relatively close together, it also increases the range of motion beyond wider-grip pull-down variations. It can be performed for low reps, such as 5-6 per set, for back strength, or for higher reps for size.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: The reverse lunge is a lower-body exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. The reverse lunge places more emphasis on the glutes than other lunge variations.

name: Reverse Nordic Curl
description: The reverse Nordic curl kneels tall and hinges the whole body backward from the knees, loading the quads through a deep stretch while the hips stay extended. Keep the hips locked forward and move slowly; it is the quad's answer to the Nordic hamstring curl.

name: Reverse Plank
description: The reverse plank faces the ceiling, supported on the hands and heels with the body straight. It strengthens the posterior chain through the glutes, hamstrings and spinal erectors while opening the chest and shoulders; push the hips high and keep the neck relaxed.

name: Reverse Plank Dips
description: The reverse plank dip lowers and raises the hips from a reverse plank by bending and straightening the elbows, training the triceps through an unusual extended-shoulder angle. Keep the hips high and the chest open; the shoulders should feel the stretch, not strain.

name: Reverse Tabletop Hip Pulses
description: The reverse tabletop hip pulses lift and lower the hips in small pulses from a reverse tabletop, hammering the glutes while the shoulders hold the bridge. Keep the shins vertical and the chest open; squeeze the glutes at the top of every pulse.

name: Reverse Tabletop Hold
description: The reverse tabletop hold bridges on hands and feet with the shins vertical and the torso flat, holding the hips at tabletop height. It trains glute and shoulder endurance and opens the front of the shoulders; keep the wrists under the shoulders and squeeze the glutes to hold.

name: Revolved Chair Pose
description: Revolved chair pose twists a chair squat, pressing the hands together and hooking one elbow outside the opposite knee. The legs hold the squat isometrically while the spine rotates; lengthen on the inhale and deepen the twist on the exhale.

name: Revolved Crescent Lunge
description: Revolved crescent lunge adds a spinal twist to the high lunge, bringing opposite hands together beside the front foot or in prayer at the chest. It is a balance and rotation drill that opens the thoracic spine while the legs hold the stance.

name: Ring Dead Hang
description: The ring dead hang hangs from gymnastic rings with straight arms, adding instability that ordinary bar hangs lack. The grip and shoulder stabilizers work overtime to control the rings; keep the body quiet and the rings from drifting.

name: Ring Dips
description: The ring dip is an upper-body strength exercise performed on gymnastic rings. It targets the muscles of the chest, triceps, and shoulders, but is also quite taxing to the core. It is generally considered to be more difficult than dips performed on parallel bars. It is common in gymnastics training and CrossFit workouts, but is also a simple way to make dips more challenging for any strength athlete.

name: Ring Face Pull
description: The ring face pull leans back holding the rings and pulls the hands apart toward the ears, training the rear delts and rotator cuff against bodyweight. The rings' instability doubles the stabilizer demand; keep the body straight from head to heel and finish with the knuckles beside the ears.

name: Ring Muscle-Up
description: The ring muscle up pulls from a hang below the rings to a support position above them, the rings adding instability to every phase. The transition demands a deep pull and a fast turn of the elbows; train high pulls and slow transitions before stringing full reps.

name: Ring Push-Up
description: The ring push up performs a push-up with the hands on unstable rings, forcing the chest, shoulders and core to control the wobble through the whole range. Keep the rings from drifting apart and the body in one line; expect fewer reps than the floor version, and that is the point.

name: Ring Row
description: The ring row leans back holding the rings and rows the chest up to the hands, an adjustable bodyweight horizontal pull. Walk the feet forward to make it harder, keep the body rigid like a plank and pull the rings to the ribs; it scales from beginner to brutally hard.

name: Rings Inverted Row
description: The rings inverted row hangs beneath the rings with the body straight and rows the chest to the rings, the unstable version of the inverted row. Keep the hips in line with the shoulders and the rings from flaring; the wobble under load is what builds the stabilizers.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: The barbell stiff-legged deadlift targets the hamstrings, glutes, lower and upper back, as well as the core. It is a popular accessory movement for the deadlift, but also a muscle-building hamstring movement.

name: Rope Climb
description: The rope climb is an exercise that is used commonly in CrossFit workouts and as a test of upper-body strength. It was even contested at the Olympics in the early 20th century. It targets a wide range of upper-body musculature, including the hands and forearms, shoulders, biceps, lats (latissimus dorsi), and core.

name: Rowing Machine
description: The rowing machine drives legs, then body, then arms to move the handle, and reverses the order on the recovery. Done well it is a full-body conditioning tool that spares the joints; drive with the hips, keep the lower back long and resist racing the flywheel.

name: Running
description: Running is steady-state locomotion at whatever pace the legs can hold, building aerobic capacity, calf and quad endurance and bone density. Land under the hips with a quick, light cadence and increase volume gradually; it pairs with strength work rather than replacing it.

name: Russian Twist
description: The Russian twist is an exercise targeting the abdominals and the obliques. Beginning from a position that resembles stopping midway through a sit-up, it involves twisting side to side. It can be performed with body weight alone or while holding a weight plate or other object. It is performed by alternating sides with each rep and can be done for time or for a specific number of reps as part of the ab-focused portion of any workout.

name: Scapular Pull Ups
description: The scapular pull up hangs from a bar and pulls the shoulder blades down and together without bending the elbows, lifting the body a few inches. It is the foundation drill of all pulling work; keep the arms straight and let the lats do the lifting.

name: Scissor Kicks
description: The scissor kick lies on the back and alternates small vertical kicks with the straight legs, holding the low abs under constant tension. Keep the lower back pressed into the floor; if it arches, raise the legs higher. Small, fast, controlled kicks.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
description: The seated barbell overhead press presses from an upright bench, removing leg drive so the shoulders do every bit of the work. Keep the lower back against the pad and the bar path just in front of the face; expect the strictest overhead strength test in the rack.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: The cable seated row is a popular exercise to train the muscles of the upper back, including the lats (latissimus dorsi), traps, rhomboids, and rear deltoids, using a cable stack. It also targets the biceps to a lesser degree. The cable row can work well in a variety of rep-ranges, but is most popular in muscle-building workouts or as an accessory movement for strength workouts.

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: The machine seated calf raise is an exercise targeting the calf muscles of the lower leg, particularly the soleus muscle. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set, and occasionally for very high burnout-focused sets of 50-100 total reps.

name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
description: The seated dumbbell biceps curl is a standard exercise for building bigger biceps. While dumbbell biceps curls can be performed standing, this version involves sitting on a bench.

name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: The seated dumbbell lateral raise is an exercise that targets the shoulder muscles, particularly the medial or middle head of the deltoids. Performing it on a bench helps enforce strict form and eliminate swinging or using momentum to move the weights. Lateral raise variations are usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of the upper-body or shoulder-focused portion of a workout.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: The seated dumbbell shoulder press is a popular exercise for building muscle and strength in the shoulders. The triceps also work hard in this lift. Many lifters find using dumbbells to be more comfortable and shoulder-friendly for this press variation than a barbell. This can be the primary pressing movement on an upper-body or shoulder day, or an effective accessory movement later in a workout.

name: Seated Dumbbell Tricep Extension
description: The seated dumbbell tricep extension lowers a bell behind the head from an upright seat, the back support removing any temptation to arch. Keep the elbows narrow and pointing forward and let the bell sink deep behind the head; the triceps work hardest in the bottom half.

name: Seated Forward Fold
description: The seated forward fold extends the legs and hinges the chest toward the toes, stretching the hamstrings and lower back. Lead with the sternum and keep the spine long; holding the feet or shins with a flat back beats yanking the head down.

name: Seated Leg Curl
description: The leg curl is a popular machine-based exercise for the legs, particularly the hamstrings. It comes in seated and lying varieties, but the seated leg curl machine is more common in commercial gyms. Leg curl variations are usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a leg pre-exhaust or as a muscle-building movement for lower-body training.

name: Seated Smith Machine Shoulder Press
description: The seated Smith machine shoulder press presses the guided bar overhead from an upright bench. The vertical track removes stabilization work, so the delts and triceps can be loaded strictly; set the bench so the bar descends just in front of the face.

name: Seated Spinal Twist
description: The seated spinal twist plants one foot outside the opposite knee and rotates the upright torso toward it. Lengthen the spine on the inhale and rotate a little more on each exhale; it mobilizes the thoracic spine and the hips together.

name: Seated Straddle Stretch
description: The seated straddle stretch opens the legs into a wide V and folds the chest toward the floor. Hinge from the hips with a long spine and walk the hands forward slowly; the adductors respond to patience far better than to force.

name: Side Lunge
description: The side lunge steps wide to one side and sinks the hip back over the bent leg while the other leg straightens, training the legs in the frontal plane. Keep the bent knee over the shoe and the chest up; push the floor away to return rather than flopping up.

name: Side Lying Hip Adduction
description: The side-lying hip adduction lifts the bottom leg against the floor from a side-lying position, isolating the inner thigh of the down leg. Keep the top knee bent and planted in front; small, controlled lifts with the toe pointed forward.

name: Side Plank
description: The side plank is a popular isometric abdominal exercise focusing on the oblique muscles, as well as the transversus abdominis or deep core muscles. It is sometimes paired with the curl up and bird dog as the “McGill big three” for core strength and stability. It is performed for time and can work in a warm-up or in the core-focused portion of any workout.

name: Side Plank Leg Lift Hold
description: The side plank leg lift hold raises the top leg off the bottom one inside a side plank and keeps it there. It stacks a glute-medius challenge on top of the obliques' isometric work; if the hips sag, return to a plain side plank first.

name: Side Plank with Leg Lift
description: The side plank with leg lift holds a side plank while raising the top leg, stacking a glute medius challenge onto the obliques' isometric hold. Keep the hips high and the body in one plane; if the hips sag, earn the leg lift back with plain side planks first.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
description: The side-lying hip abduction lifts the top leg from a side-lying position, the classic glute medius builder. Keep the leg in line with the body rather than drifting forward, and the pelvis still; the range is small and the burn is the point.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction Hold
description: The side-lying hip abduction hold keeps the top leg lifted from a side-lying position, isolating the hip abductors isometrically. Keep the leg in line with the body rather than drifting forward, and the pelvis still; the burn should sit deep in the side of the hip.

name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction Hold
description: The side-lying hip adduction hold lifts the bottom leg against the floor from a side-lying position and holds it up, targeting the inner thigh. Keep the hips stacked; the bottom adductors work hard for such a small range.

name: Side-Lying Lateral Raise
description: The side-lying lateral raise raises a bell from a side-lying position, loading the deltoid of the bottom arm through its strictest arc. The floor removes all swing; raise to just past vertical and lower slowly, since the bottom half of the range is where this version earns its keep.

name: Single Arm Tricep Pushdown
description: The single-arm tricep pushdown extends one arm down against a cable, keeping constant tension from the very top of the rep. Keep the upper arm glued to the side and squeeze fully at lockout; the free hand can steady the torso.

name: Single Dumbbell Svend Press
description: The single dumbbell Svend press squeezes the top of a bell between the palms and presses it out at chest height, an isometric pec squeeze layered onto a press. Keep the squeeze constant, since the press range can be short; the chest should tremble before the arms do.

name: Single Leg Calf Raise
description: The single-leg calf raise drives one heel up at a time, doubling the load on each calf without any equipment. Hold a wall for balance only, keep the knee straight and work through the full stretch at the bottom; the free foot can hook behind the working ankle.

name: Single Leg Extension
description: The single-leg leg extension is a popular machine-based exercise for the legs, particularly the quadriceps. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a leg pre-exhaust or as a muscle-building movement for lower-body training. Performing it one leg a time allows you to focus on the mind-muscle connection of each leg and address muscle imbalances.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
description: The single-leg glute bridge is a lower-body exercise that targets the glutes, lower back, and hamstrings. It is performed one side at a time.

name: Single Leg Lying Leg Curl
description: The single-leg lying leg curl is a popular machine-based exercise for the legs, particularly the hamstrings. It is similar to the seated leg curl, but the open hip angle in the lying leg curl may incorporate more glute and calf activation. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a leg pre-exhaust or as a muscle-building movement for lower-body training. Performing it one leg a time allows you to focus on the mind-muscle connection of each leg and address muscle imbalances.

name: Single Leg Press
description: The single-leg leg press is an exercise targeting the quadriceps one leg at a time. Many lifters prefer the leg press to squatting for several reasons, including the perception that it’s safer for the spine.

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: The single-leg dumbbell Romanian deadlift is a movement targeting the muscles of the hamstrings, glutes, and back. The difference between a Romanian deadlift and a stiff-legged deadlift is the amount of knee bend. The knees are only slightly bent in a stiff-legged deadlift, while they bend more in a Romanian deadlift. Single-leg deadlifts are generally performed for low to moderate reps, such as 8-10 reps per set, with a focus on maximizing the hamstring stretch rather than moving heavy weight. If balance is a challenge, this movement is still very effective if performed while holding on to a stable object for support.

name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
description: The single-arm chest-supported dumbbell row rows one bell from a chest-down bench position, letting each side of the back work through its own range with zero momentum. Pull the elbow past the ribs and rotate the shoulder blade at the top; the pad keeps the spine honest.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension
description: The single-arm dumbbell overhead tricep extension lowers one bell behind the head, letting the elbow track its own natural path while the triceps work in isolation. Keep the upper arm vertical and close to the ear; support the working arm with the free hand at the elbow.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
description: The single-arm dumbbell row is a popular exercise for building the latissimus dorsi, or lat, muscles of the back. It is most often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per arm or more, as part of a muscle-building upper-body or back-focused portion of a workout.

name: Single-Arm Hammer Curl
description: The single-arm hammer curl curls one bell with a neutral grip, letting each arm work without the stronger side hiding. Keep the elbow pinned to the ribs and squeeze the bell at the top; the wrist stays locked as if swinging a hammer.

name: Single-Arm Machine Shoulder Press
description: The single-arm machine shoulder press presses one handle overhead from a fixed seat, training each side on its own. The machine stabilizes the path so the working shoulder can focus on pressing; keep the torso upright and resist the twist toward the loaded side.

name: Single-Arm Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise
description: The single-arm plate-loaded lateral raise raises one lever at a time through the machine's arc, letting each delt work without the stronger side hiding. Keep the elbow slightly bent and the torso still; lighter than the two-arm version is normal.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge Hold
description: The single-leg glute bridge is a lower-body exercise that targets the glutes, lower back, and hamstrings. It is performed one side at a time.

name: Sit-Ups
description: The sit-up is a popular bodyweight exercise focused on the abdominal muscles. It has also been used as part of military, tactical, and scholastic fitness tests for many years. It can be performed for time or reps, with the feet anchored or free, on flat ground or a bench.

name: Skull Crusher
description: The EZ-bar skullcrusher is a popular exercise targeting the triceps muscles. The EZ-bar is used more often than a straight bar. As for the name, that’s worst-case scenario. The bar should actually come down behind the head. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps as part of an upper body or arms-focused workout. No need to chase a 1RM on this move!

name: Sled Row
description: The sled row anchors a rope or straps to a loaded sled and rows the body toward it, or drags the sled hand over hand. It is a joint-friendly horizontal pull that loads the back without shearing the spine; keep the hips low and drive the elbows past the ribs.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
description: The Smith machine bench press is a machine-based movement targeting the chest. The Smith machine mimics a barbell but provides more stability. This movement can be programmed in low reps for strength or higher reps for muscle and strength endurance. It is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a chest or upper-body focused workout.

name: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
description: The Smith machine bent-over row is an upper-body exercise targeting the muscles of the back, particularly the lats (latissimus dorsi). This movement can be programmed in low reps for strength or higher reps for muscle and strength endurance. It is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of an upper-body or back-focused workout.

name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat
description: The Smith machine Bulgarian split squat sets the rear foot on a bench with the bar guiding a perfectly vertical path, letting the front leg take all the load. The fixed bar removes balance from the equation, so more load reaches the quads and glutes of the working leg.

name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
