description: The Smith machine standing calf raise is a machine-based exercise targeting the muscles of the calves, particularly the gastrocnemius or upper calf muscle. It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of the lower-body portion of a workout.

name: Smith Machine Decline Bench Press
description: The Smith machine decline bench press is a machine-based exercise targeting the chest muscles, particularly the lower pectoral muscles. The Smith machine mimics a barbell but provides more stability. This movement is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a chest or upper-body workout.

name: Smith Machine Front Squat
description: The Smith machine front squat is a machine-based exercise targeting the muscles of the lower body. The Smith machine mimics a barbell but provides more stability. This movement can be programmed in low reps for strength or higher reps for muscle and strength endurance. It is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a full-body or lower-body workout.

name: Smith Machine Good Morning
description: The Smith machine good morning hinges at the hips under a guided bar on the back, loading the hamstrings and erectors through a controlled bow. The fixed path makes the pattern safer to learn than the free-bar version; keep the knees soft and the spine long.

name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
description: The Smith machine hip thrust drives the hips to full extension against a bar that travels straight up over them. The fixed path removes the balancing act of the free-bar version, so the glutes can be loaded hard and progressively.

name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
description: The Smith machine incline bench press is a machine-based movement targeting the chest, particularly the upper chest. The Smith machine mimics a barbell but provides more stability. This movement can be programmed in low reps for strength or higher reps for muscle and strength endurance. It is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a chest or upper-body focused workout.

name: Smith Machine Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
description: The Smith machine reverse-grip bent-over row rows the guided bar with palms up, shifting emphasis toward the lats and lower biceps. The fixed path takes balance out of the hinge; keep the torso close to parallel and pull the bar to the lower ribs.

name: Smith Machine Reverse Lunge
description: The Smith machine reverse lunge steps back under a guided bar, keeping the load traveling straight up and down. The fixed path spares the knees and lets balance take a back seat, which suits higher loads and stricter form.

name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
description: The Smith machine Romanian deadlift hinges under a bar locked to a vertical track, stretching the hamstrings under a guided load. The bar's path removes forward drift so the hinge stays honest; push the hips back and stop when the hamstrings run out.

name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
description: The Smith machine shoulder press is a machine-based exercise targeting the deltoid muscles. The Smith machine mimics a barbell but provides more stability. This movement can be programmed in low reps for strength or higher reps for muscle and strength endurance. It is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a shoulder or upper-body focused workout.

name: Smith Machine Shrug
description: The Smith machine shrug is an upper-body exercise targeting the traps (trapezius muscles). It is usually performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of shoulder or trap-focused training.

name: Smith Machine Split Squat
description: The Smith machine split squat holds a static split stance while the guided bar tracks straight over the midfoot. With balance handled by the machine, the front quad and glute take clean, progressive load.

name: Smith Machine Squat
description: The Smith machine back squat is a machine-based exercise targeting the muscles of the lower body. The Smith machine mimics a barbell but provides more stability. This movement can be programmed in low reps for strength or higher reps for muscle and strength endurance. It is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of a full-body or lower-body workout.

name: Smith Machine Upright Row
description: The Smith machine upright row is an upper-body exercise targeting the muscles of the traps and shoulders. This movement is often performed for moderate to high reps, such as 8-12 reps per set or more, as part of an upper-body or shoulder-focused workout.

name: Snatch
description: The snatch takes the barbell from the floor to overhead in one continuous motion, catching it in a deep overhead squat. It is the most athletic lift in the barbell catalog, demanding speed, mobility and precision in one; the bar must stay close and the punch overhead violent.

name: Sphinx Pose
description: Sphinx pose lies on the forearms with the elbows under the shoulders and the chest lifted into a gentle backbend. It restores the lumbar curve after sitting and prepares the spine for deeper extension; press the forearms down and keep the glutes soft.

name: Spider Curl
description: The spider curl curls two bells from a chest-down incline position with the arms hanging vertical, isolating the biceps at their shortest position. With the shoulder fixed and the elbows unsupported, nothing can swing; squeeze hard at the top and lower for a three-count.

name: Split Jerk
description: The split jerk drives the bar overhead with a dip and a split of the legs, dropping under the bar to catch it with straight arms. It moves more overhead weight than any press; recover the feet front, back, together, and keep the front shin vertical.

name: Split Squat
description: The split squat holds a static split stance and sinks the back knee toward the floor, training each leg in place without the step of a lunge. Keep the torso tall and the front heel down; the back knee hovers just above the floor at the bottom.

name: Spoto Press
description: The Spoto press is a variation of the popular barbell exercise the bench press that builds strength and muscle in the chest, triceps, and shoulders. It differs from the bench press in that the lifter pauses for a few seconds at the bottom of the movement before pressing the bar back up. This pause removes all momentum and increases the time under tension for the chest and shoulder muscles to help develop upper-body musculature and strength.

name: Stability Ball Hip Bridge
description: The stability ball hip bridge rests the feet on a stability ball and bridges the hips up, adding an unstable platform to the glute bridge. Keep the ball from drifting and the hips level; the hamstrings and glutes work overtime to steady the ball.

name: Stability Ball Knee Tuck
description: The stability ball knee tuck pulls the knees toward the chest from a high plank with the feet on the ball, rolling the ball in with the core. Keep the shoulders stacked over the wrists and the hips from sagging; the ball should move because the abs curled, not because the arms pulled.

name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
description: The exercise ball leg curl is an exercise targeting the hamstrings. In particular, it targets the knee flexion function of the hamstrings, as opposed to deadlift variations, which target the other hamstring function, hip flexion. Many lifters opt for this exercise when they don't have access to a lying leg curl machine, but it is worth considering even if you already do machine curls.

name: Stability Ball Push-Up
description: The stability ball push-up sets the feet or shins on a stability ball during a push-up, adding instability that forces the core to lock the body into one plank. Keep the hands planted and the ball quiet; the wobblier the ball, the better the core works.

name: Stability Ball Push-Up (Hands on Ball)
description: The stability ball push-up with hands on the ball sets the palms on the unstable ball itself, demanding enormous shoulder stability through the press. Keep the elbows tracking back and the ball from sliding; go narrow in range before chasing depth.

name: Stability Ball Wall Squat
description: The stability ball wall squat rolls a ball between the back and the wall as the hips sink into a squat, guiding the spine through a smooth, supported arc. Keep the feet far enough forward that the knees stay behind the toes; the ball keeps the back tall and honest.

name: Stair Climber
description: The stair climber is a popular cardio machine found in most commercial gyms. Along with burning a ton of calories, the stair climber also helps build strength in the lower body, especially the glutes. It can work well at higher speeds for interval-style conditioning training, but also works well at slower paces for steady-state cardio.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: The standing calf raise is a popular movement to target the calf muscles of the lower leg, and in particular the gastrocnemius muscles. When unweighted, it is usually performed for high reps or for time.

name: Standing Calf Stretch
description: The standing calf stretch braces the hands on a wall and steps one foot back, pressing that heel into the floor. A straight back knee biases the gastrocnemius while a bent knee reaches the soleus; hold each version for 20 to 30 seconds.

name: Standing Forward Fold
description: The standing forward fold hinges at the hips and lets the torso hang toward the floor, releasing the hamstrings and back. Bend the knees as much as needed to keep the fold comfortable; gravity does the stretching, so no pulling is required.

name: Standing Forward Fold to Half Lift
description: This flow moves between a standing forward fold and a half lift with a flat back, teaching the hinge and lengthening the hamstrings in both directions. Flow with the breath; the flat-backed half position is where the hinge pattern is trained.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
description: The standing quad stretch is a simple exercise designed to stretch the quadriceps, the big muscles that cover most of the thighs. This is a static stretch, meaning it’s usually performed by holding the stretched position for a certain length of time.

name: Standing Side Bend
description: The standing side bend stretch is a stretching exercise targeting the obliques, the muscles that run along the side of the core. It is a common inclusion in dynamic warm-ups for the upper body, but can also be performed to help \"limber up\" for lifting or athletics anytime.

name: Standing Side Bend Flow
description: The standing side bend flow reaches one arm overhead and leans side to side in a continuous rhythm, opening the obliques and the space between the ribs and hip. Keep both feet grounded and the hips still so the bend happens along the spine.

name: Standing Split
description: The standing split folds forward and lifts one leg toward the ceiling as high as the hamstring allows. It is an intense hamstring stretch of the standing leg and a hip-flexor stretch of the lifted one; keep the hips level rather than chasing leg height.

name: Stationary Bike
description: The stationary bike is a popular cardio machine found in most commercial gyms. Along with burning a ton of calories, the stationary bike also helps develop the lower body. Stationary bikes come in multiple variations, ranging from ones that resemble riding a bike, to recumbent bikes, to fan bikes that work both the arms and the legs. No matter the variation, a stationary bike can work well at higher speeds for interval-style conditioning training, but also works well at slower paces for steady-state cardio.

name: Step Ups
description: The step up drives up onto a box or bench from a standing start, training each leg through a full, functional range. Keep the whole foot on the box and push through the heel rather than bouncing off the trailing toe; step down softly under control.

name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
description: The stiff-leg deadlift hinges at the hips with only a soft knee bend, loading the hamstrings through a longer stretch than the conventional pull. Keep the bar close to the legs and the spine long; the range ends where the hamstrings stop, not where the plates touch.

name: Straight Bar Dips
description: The straight bar dip dips between two parallel bars or on a single straight bar with a pronated grip, a less familiar hand position that loads the chest and triceps afresh. Keep the shoulders down and the lean forward; the unusual grip makes even strong dippers work.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: The straight-arm bar pull-down is a variation of the straight-arm lat pull-down performed using a cable stack machine. It can either be performed in an athletic upright stance, or slightly bent-over. It both stretches and contracts the muscles of the lats (latissimus dorsi) as well as providing additional activation to the other upper back muscles and the core. Because the triceps are also isometrically involved in the movement, it is usually performed for higher reps, like 8-15 reps or above.

name: Straight-Bar Cable Front Raise
description: The straight-bar cable front raise raises a bar from a low pulley to shoulder height in front of the body, loading the front delts under constant tension. Keep the arms nearly straight and the torso still; resist the cable all the way down.

name: Strict Curl
description: The strict curl curls a barbell with the back flat against a wall, removing every ounce of hip and shoulder drive. Keep the elbows pinned and the head, shoulders and glutes touching the wall; it is the purest test of biceps strength there is.

name: Suitcase Carry
description: The suitcase carry walks with a single heavy bell held at one side like a suitcase, forcing the obliques to keep the spine vertical. Stay tall and do not lean away from the load; it is one of the simplest and best anti-lateral-flexion drills.

name: Sumo Deadlift
description: The sumo deadlift is a compound movement in which the feet are set in a wide stance with toes pointed out and grip is placed inside of the legs. It is allowed to be performed instead of conventional deadlifts in most powerlifting competitions. The sumo deadlift targets the hamstrings, glutes, and upper back/traps, but also has a greater emphasis on stretching and strengthening the adductor and hip muscles due to the wide stance.

name: Sumo Squat
description: The sumo squat squats with a very wide stance and the toes turned out, shifting load toward the adductors, glutes and inner quads. Keep the knees tracking over the toes and the torso tall; sink between the hips rather than folding forward.

name: Superman
description: The Superman is a bodyweight exercise that consists of isometric holds in an extended spine position. It targets the muscles of the posterior chain, including the muscles of the glutes, spinal erectors, and upper back. It can be performed as part of a dynamic warm-up, or for muscle activation or mobility anytime.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
description: The supine spinal twist lies on the back and drops the knees to one side while the shoulders stay heavy on the floor. It unwinds the lower back and chest after training; rest the top knee on a block if the floor is too far away.

name: Supine Windshield Wipers
description: The supine windshield wiper lies on the back with the arms wide and sweeps the straight legs side to side like wipers, rotating through the trunk against gravity. Keep the shoulders pinned to the floor; the legs travel and the chest does not. Bend the knees to make it easier.

name: Supported Shoulderstand
description: The supported shoulderstand lifts the legs and hips overhead with the hands supporting the back, resting the weight on the shoulders. It is a gentle inversion that stretches the neck and upper back; enter and exit slowly and keep the head still.

name: Svend Press
description: The Svend press is an exercise where the chest is targeted by performing presses while squeezing two weight plates together. It is usually performed for relatively high reps with light weights as an accessory movement to the bench press or as a burnout movement on chest day.

name: T-Bar Row
description: The T-bar row rows a landmine-loaded bar from a hinged stance, pulling the weighted end to the chest with both hands. The anchored end removes balance demands so the lats and mid-back can be loaded hard; keep the hinge still and the chest proud.

name: Thoracic Bridge
description: The thoracic bridge pushes the hips up while reaching one arm overhead to rotate the upper back through the bridge. It restores rotation to a stiff mid-back and stretches the chest; keep the supporting shoulder stacked over the wrist.

name: Thread the Needle
description: Thread the needle slides one arm under the chest from all fours, resting the shoulder and ear on the floor. It rotates the thoracic spine and stretches between the shoulder blades; press the top hand down to deepen gently.

name: Thread the Needle Flow
description: The thread the needle flow alternates reaching one arm to the ceiling and threading it under the body, opening and closing thoracic rotation in rhythm. Move with the breath; it is a reliable warm-up before any pressing, throwing or rotational work.

name: Three-Legged Downward Dog
description: The three-legged downward dog lifts one leg toward the ceiling from a downward dog, loading the standing hip and opening the lifted one. Keep the hips as square as the hamstring allows and press firmly through both hands.

name: Thruster
description: The thruster chains a front squat into an overhead press in one continuous movement, using the squat's drive to punch the bar up. It is the ultimate full-body conditioning lift; ride the bar down into the next squat smoothly and breathe at the top.

name: Toes to Bar
description: The hanging toes-to-bar is an advanced abdominal exercise in which the lifter touches their feet to a pull-up bar. There are many ways to perform this movement: strict or swinging, arms completely straight or slightly bent, legs straight or bent, each providing unique benefits and challenges. Initially, it may be a difficult move to do for a single rep, but once you build the requisite core, lat, and shoulder strength, it can be performed for higher reps.

name: Treadmill Running
description: Treadmill running is a popular cardiovascular exercise performed on a machine that is available in most gyms. Performing this exercise on a treadmill allows you to adjust the speed of your running and, depending on the machine, perform it on an adjustable incline. Many machines also have built-in heart rate monitors and timers to help you track your progress.

name: Tree Pose
description: Tree pose balances on one leg with the other foot pressed to the inner thigh and the hands in prayer overhead. Press the foot and thigh into each other and fix the gaze on a still point; wobbling is the drill working.

name: Triangle Pose
description: Triangle pose stands in a wide stance and tips the torso over the front leg, stacking the hands vertically toward the floor and ceiling. Lengthen both sides of the waist equally; the stretch belongs to the hamstrings and the side body together.

name: TRX Bicep Curl
description: The TRX bicep curl leans back holding the straps and curls the body up toward the anchors by flexing the elbows, using bodyweight as the resistance. Keep the body rigid like a plank and the elbows fixed at shoulder height; walk the feet in to add load.

name: TRX Chest Press
description: The TRX chest press holds the straps and lowers the body toward the hands in a push-up against the suspension trainer. Keep the straps under tension and the body in one line; the further the feet walk back, the harder the press.

name: TRX Face Pull
description: The TRX face pull leans back and pulls the straps apart toward the ears, training the rear delts and rotator cuff with bodyweight. Keep the body straight and the elbows high; the finish has the hands wide and level with the head.

name: TRX Hamstring Curl
description: The TRX hamstring curl lies on the back with the heels in the straps and curls the hips up while pulling the heels under the body, a leg curl and bridge in one. Keep the hips high throughout the rep; the slower the pull-in, the more the hamstrings earn.

name: TRX Lunge
description: The TRX lunge rests the rear foot in a strap while lunging forward on the front leg, the suspended rear leg adding range and balance demand. Keep the torso tall and the front knee tracking over the shoe; the strap pulls the rear hip into a deeper stretch.

name: TRX Pistol Squat
description: The TRX pistol squat uses the straps as a balance aid while descending on one leg, letting the athlete learn the depth before owning the balance. Keep the free leg long and the heel down; lighten the grip gradually until the straps carry nothing.

name: TRX Plank
description: The TRX plank sets the feet in the straps and holds a plank with the body in one line. The unstable suspension forces the core to fight rotation and sagging simultaneously; keep the shoulders away from the ears and the straps quiet.

name: TRX Row
description: The TRX row leans back holding the straps and rows the chest up to the hands, the most adjustable horizontal pull in bodyweight training. Keep the body rigid and the straps quiet; walk the feet forward or raise them to scale the load.

name: TRX Side Plank
description: The TRX side plank holds a side plank with the feet suspended in the straps. The obliques and hip stabilizers work against the straps' drift; keep the body long and the bottom shoulder packed.

name: TRX Squat
description: The TRX squat squats while holding the straps, using them for balance and assistance on the way down and up. Keep the grip light, since the legs should do the work the straps merely steady; sit back and down between the heels.

name: TRX Triceps Extension
description: The TRX triceps extension faces away from the anchors and extends the elbows to press the body up from a flexed-arm position, a bodyweight skull crusher. Keep the body straight and the head passing between the hands; the closer the feet to the anchors, the harder the lockout.

name: TRX Y-Fly
description: The TRX Y-fly leans back holding the straps and raises the arms overhead into a Y, training the lower traps and rear delts through a long lever. Keep the body straight and the elbows soft; the shoulder blades do the lifting, not the arms.

name: Upward-Facing Dog
description: Upward-facing dog presses the chest up from the floor with straight arms and the thighs hovering, opening the front of the body. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears and push the tops of the feet into the floor to spare the lower back.

name: V Ups
description: The V-up lies flat and lifts the straight legs and torso together until the hands reach the feet, folding the body into a V at the top. Keep the legs and arms long and the movement controlled; the lower back should stay light on the floor on the way down.

name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
description: The V-bar lat pulldown uses a close neutral handle to pull the weight down to the chest, emphasizing the lower lats and a strong squeeze. Keep the torso near upright and drive the elbows down toward the hips rather than pulling with the hands.

name: V-Bar Tricep Pushdown
description: The V-bar tricep pushdown uses the angled V handle to press down against a high pulley, angling the hands naturally outward. The neutral grip spares the wrists and elbows; keep the elbows fixed and finish each rep with a full lockout.

name: V-Sit
description: The V-sit balances on the sitting bones with the straight legs and torso forming a V, a static core hold that loads the hip flexors and abdominals together. Keep the chest proud and the spine long; if the shoulders round, bring the legs closer to the floor.

name: Walking
description: Walking is the lowest-cost conditioning there is: a brisk, steady pace that builds the aerobic base and aids recovery between harder sessions. Keep the pace honest enough to raise the breath; hills or a weighted vest add load without impact.

name: Walking Lunge
description: The walking lunge is a lower-body exercise that targets the glutes, quads, and hamstrings while challenging stability and balance. It can be performed for reps, time, or distance in the lower-body portion of any workout.

name: Wall Push Ups
description: The wall push up presses away from a wall while standing, the gentlest push-up progression there is. Keep the body in one straight line from head to heel and the elbows at about 45 degrees; walk the feet further from the wall to add load.

name: Wall Sit
description: The wall sit is an exercise targeting the quadriceps and core muscle. It involves descending into a squat position while leaning against a wall, then holding that position for a predetermined length of time. It's a classic leg endurance-building exercise for basketball players and gymnasts.

name: Warrior I
description: Warrior I squares the hips forward in a long lunge with the arms reaching overhead. It opens the hip flexors of the back leg while the front leg, core and shoulders hold the frame; keep the back heel heavy or lifted consistently on one side.

name: Warrior II
description: Warrior II holds a wide bent-knee stance with the arms extended in a T and the gaze over the front hand. It builds endurance through the quads and hips while opening the chest; sink the front thigh toward parallel and keep the torso upright.

name: Warrior III
description: Warrior III balances on one leg with the torso and the other leg forming a horizontal T. The standing glute and hamstring carry everything while the core keeps the spine long; reach through the back heel as actively as the fingertips.

name: Weighted Dips
description: Weighted dips add a plate or dumbbell to the standard chest dip, pushing the triceps and lower chest into serious overload. Keep the lean forward, the elbows tracking back and the range honest; add load only once bodyweight reps are comfortable.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
description: The weighted pull-up is a more advanced variation of the pull-up exercise in which the lifter adds extra weight to their body. Options for adding weight include a dip belt, weighted vest, chains, a dumbbell placed between the feet or legs, or looping a kettlebell over the foot. Like other pull-up variations, the weighted pull-up builds strength and muscle in the upper back, biceps, and core.

name: Weighted Wall Crunch
description: The weighted wall crunch lies with the legs up a wall and crunches a plate or dumbbell from the chest toward the feet. The wall fixes the hips so the abs do the whole job; curl the ribs toward the pelvis rather than pulling the head.

name: Wide Grip Pull Ups
description: The wide-grip pull up hangs with the hands well outside the shoulders and pulls the chest to the bar, shifting the load toward the upper lats and teres major. Keep the shoulders from shrugging and the range full; a slightly shorter chin-over-bar path is normal at this width.

name: Wide Grip Push Ups
description: The wide-grip push up spreads the hands well outside the shoulders, biasing the outer chest while shortening the triceps' role. Keep the body in one plank and the elbows from flaring too far; the wider the hands, the more careful the shoulder position.

name: Wide Grip Seated Cable Row
description: The wide-grip seated cable row rows a wide bar to the upper abdomen with the elbows flared, shifting emphasis toward the rear delts and mid-back. Sit tall, pull the shoulder blades together at the finish and keep the torso from rocking with the weight.

name: Wide-Grip Bench Press
description: The wide-grip bench press is a compound exercise targeting the chest and, to a lesser extent, the triceps. The main difference between this exercise and the standard bench press is that the hands are placed farther apart on the bar. Many lifters find they can handle more weight going wide than with narrower grips, although it's also worth noting that plenty of banged-up lifters have said benching with a wide grip may also have contributed to their shoulder injuries and pain. The wide-grip bench is often used as a chest-building movement in chest or upper-body workouts, or as an accessory movement for the traditional bench press.

name: Wide-Legged Forward Fold
description: The wide-legged forward fold stands with the feet wide and folds the torso down between the legs, stretching the adductors and hamstrings together. Keep the weight in the mid-foot and the spine long; hands to the floor or to the ankles both work.

name: Wide-Stance Leg Press
description: The wide-stance leg press spreads the feet high and wide on the platform, opening the hips toward the adductors and glutes. Depth still rules; go as deep as the pelvis allows without lifting off the pad, and drive through the whole foot.

name: Wrist Roller
description: The wrist roller winds a weighted rope up by rolling a handle over and over, burning the forearms through their full range. Roll in both directions and resist on the way down; it is the classic finisher for grip day.

name: Zottman Curl
description: The Zottman curl curls a bell with the palm up, then rotates at the top and lowers it with the palm down, training the biceps on the way up and the brachialis and extensors on the way down. Keep the rotation smooth at the top and the lowering slow; the eccentric is the point.
